descriptions.github:5692081394: Developed and tested on macOS and Linux. Nothing deliberately excludes Windows, but four things make it unlikely to work there today — and none are covered by tests. Priority: nice to have. Not blocking; filed so the gaps are written down rather than rediscovered. 1. The interpreter default is wrong for Windows gleanCodeBridge.pythonPath defaults to python3 . On Windows the conventional launcher is py (or python ), and python3 commonly resolves to a Microsoft Store stub that opens the Store instead of running anything. A first-run failure here looks like a hang or an unrelated error. 2. The interpreter resolver has no platform branching src/pythonBridge.ts looks for an installed zipapp at /.local/bin/glean and bare glean on PATH — both POSIX conventions. There is no process.platform check anywhere in the resolver, and no handling of .exe or Windows script shims. 3. The one-line…
descriptions.github:5692072666: Problem. Some error messages say what failed but not what to do. Examples from crates/soroban-failure-rpc/src/error.rs : - failed to decode envelopeXdr as XDR: gives no hint about the usual causes. - malformed response: does not say which part of the response was unexpected. TransactionNotFound already explains the likely cause (retention window), and is the model to follow. Why it matters. A developer who sees one of these messages must work out the cause alone. A sentence naming the likely cause saves that time. Scope. - Improve the Display text of existing variants, and the text of the places that construct BadResponse and Xdr , so each message names the field or step and a likely cause. - Keep every claim about cause hedged to what the code can show. Non-goals. - No new error variants. - No change to behaviour, exit codes, or retry logic. - No change to public enum shapes…

Acceptance criteria. - cargo run -p soroban-failure-analysis --example…

A maintainer needs repeatable local measurements before judging a change. Absolute timings in CI would be flaky and are not wanted. Scope. - Add criterion as a dev-dependency of soroban-failure-analysis . - Add a benchmark that runs analyze() on each committed failed-transaction fixture, loaded from fixtures/ . - Document in the crate README how to run it and how to compare two runs. Non-goals. - No absolute timing thresholds. - No benchmark-based CI gate. A CI job may compile the benches ( cargo bench --no-run ), nothing more. - No optimisation in this issue. descriptions.github:5692070887: Problem. crates/soroban-failure-analysis/src/contract/wasm.rs contains a hand-written parser ( custom sections ) that reads contract WASM. That WASM is fetched from an RPC endpoint, so it is untrusted input. ContractSpec::from wasm depends on it. Neither has been fuzzed. Related. Distinct from 8, which covers the XDR decode path. The two should not be combined. Why it matters. A hostile or malformed module must produce an error, never a panic, an unbounded allocation, or a hang. Those are the properties a fuzzer can check and unit tests tend to miss. Scope. - Add a fuzz target for custom sections and ContractSpec::from wasm , using cargo-fuzz , in a fuzz/ crate excluded from the workspace. - Seed the corpus from the WASM in fixtures/contracts/ (the recorded code entries). - Any crash found becomes a regression test in wasm.rs , and is fixed in the smallest change that keeps existing…

descriptions.github:5692051383: On windows-latest , npm test starts and never finishes; runs sat for hours until cancelled. macOS and Linux pass on Node 22 and 24. CI now fails a test that runs longer than 60 seconds ( --test-timeout=60000 ) and a job after 20 minutes, so the next Windows run should name the test that hangs. Likely suspects are tests that start child processes or the local named-pipe bridge and don't close them on Windows. Windows is experimental (see 28), so this doesn't fail the build, but fixing it is the first step to supporting it.
descriptions.github:5692051131: Ctrl-] switches between the agent and the quiz. It is hard-coded in src/screen.js ( TOGGLE KEY , which also matches the kitty and xterm modifyOtherKeys forms), and some keyboard layouts and terminals make it awkward. Proposal: a switchKey setting in /.hyperfocus/config.json , for example "ctrl-]" (default) or "ctrl-g" , validated in src/config.js like the other keys, and shown wherever the help text says Ctrl-]. Config keys are a public format ( docs/FORMATS.md ): adding one is fine within 1.x; it must be optional with today's behaviour as the default.

Symptom On my home PC (Windows, keyboard plugged directly into the motherboard), the Num Lock, Caps Lock, and Scroll Lock LEDs went dark after roughly 30 to 60 minutes of normal use. Likely cause In keyboards/leyden jar/io expander.c, the IO expander is configured only once, in io expander init(). After that, io expander update state() writes the output register only when the LED state…

descriptions.github:5691887000: A camada de mapas antigos (Allmaps) já está no código e liga sozinha quando um mapa tem uma anotação de georreferenciamento IIIF. Falta o primeiro mapa. Candidato: Mappa da viação ferrea de São Paulo e partes dos estados vizinhos , de R. Heyse (organizado em 1910, publicado em 1912 pela Weiszflog Irmãos), em Princeton: Passos 1. Obter o manifesto IIIF do mapa (ou de outro mapa de 1905–1940 que mostre a Noroeste). 2. Georreferenciar no Allmaps Editor. 3. Colocar a URL da anotação em src/content/historic-maps/heyse-1912.yaml ( georef annotation ) e mudar status: georeferenced . 4. Usar o mapa para redesenhar o trecho do Tietê (hoje esquemático). Outros acervos para procurar: Biblioteca Nacional (BNDigital), David Rumsey, Arquivo Público do Estado de SP (Comissão Geográfica e Geológica).
descriptions.github:5691886291: Guatambu (aberta em 7/8/1922, desativada em 18/3/1969) ficava no leito original entre Birigui e Araçatuba. Não sabemos a posição exata: o ponto no mapa foi calculado pela quilometragem de 1960 (km 256,319, ou seja, 9,19 km depois de Birigui, no km 247,129). Giesbrecht menciona que em 2008 restava "uma velha casa de ferroviário" junto à plataforma coberta de mato. Isso pode ser identificável em imagem de satélite ou numa visita. Onde mexer: src/content/stations/guatambu.md .
descriptions.github:5691886113: A primeira estação de Birigui (aberta em 13/12/1912; prédio de 1917, demolido em 1969) ficava, segundo um depoimento citado por Giesbrecht, "no centro da cidade, a umas três quadras da igreja matriz" . Hoje o mapa a coloca no leito antigo (atual Av. José Agostinho Rossi), a 360 m da Paróquia Imaculada Conceição, com confiança baixa . O que ajudaria - planta antiga da cidade ou do pátio ferroviário; - foto aérea dos anos 1950/60 (IGC, Emplasa); - fotos antigas que mostrem a estação e algo reconhecível ao redor; - edições antigas do jornal A Verdade ; Museu Histórico de Birigui; moradores antigos. Onde mexer: src/content/stations/birigui.md → sites[id=centro].coords .

descriptions.github:5691865816: What is due parses a stored know by with date.fromisoformat , which accepts compact forms such as 20261001 on Python 3.11 and later but rejects them on 3.9 and 3.10. add itself only accepts YYYY-MM-DD , so this only affects hand-edited logs. Where plugins/decision-journal/skills/decision-journal/scripts/journal.py ( is due ); parse date already enforces the strict form. Failing scenario or evidence Verified: a hand-edited entry with "know by": "20261001" is listed by list --due on Python 3.11; on 3.9 it would be silently skipped. descriptions.github:5691839656: Problem BarChart, PieChart, and Legend support updating their content after construction. However, updates made after calling add to page() do not update the objects stored on that page. The internal group contains the replacement objects, while the page still contains the original objects. Consequently, exporting the page produces a diagram with stale data, labels, or colors. Calling add to page() again is not a reliable workaround: it adds the replacement objects without removing the old content. Reproduction The same behavior was reproduced with: PieChart.update data(): the page retains the original slices and labels. Legend.update mapping(): the page retains the original color boxes and labels. Color updates also use the same rebuild mechanism and therefore have the same underlying problem. Root cause add to page() adds each object from the internal group to the page. When an update…

descriptions.github:5691728693: Problem you're trying to solve A hosted server that acts as the signed-in user ( AuthMode=onBehalfOf ) knows who that user is. Yet the tracked changes and comments it writes carry whatever revision.author the agent put in the plan, or OfficeAgent when it put nothing. A reviewer opening the document in Word cannot tell which person's request produced a redline, and an agent can write any name it likes. The library already keeps the two identities apart ( docs/document-plans.md , "Revision identity"): - revision.author is display text, and plans may set it; - the authenticated caller goes on the audit receipt through IAuditActorProvider , and plans can never set it. The shipped MCP server registers no IAuditActorProvider , though. So its receipts carry no actor either, even when the request arrived with a user token that Entra accepted for the On-Behalf-Of exchange. Proposed shape 1…
descriptions.github:5691728574: Problem Follow-ups from review of 8928: - delete impl refuses when the recorded root identity is absent only through a separate match flag. It should refuse on an absent identity by itself. - Recording the root identity treats only a missing working directory as "no identity". PermissionError and NotADirectoryError still make environment creation raise. - The copy-on-write and Linux bubblewrap delete paths are skipped on macOS, so they have only been checked by reading the code. They should run on a Linux CI host. Proposed fix Make the absent-identity refusal local to delete impl , and handle those two errors like a missing directory. Make sure the copy-on-write and bubblewrap delete tests run in Linux CI.

descriptions.github:5691531812: What happens 1. An agent connection test for the Reasonix CLI runs reasonix acp inside a throwaway od-conn-test- temp dir ( apps/daemon/src/connectionTest.ts ), with cwd pointed at the temp dir. 2. The probe sends a real smoke prompt, so the Reasonix CLI starts an actual session — and persists it into the user's real state home ( %APPDATA%\reasonix\sessions\ .jsonl ), because the test isolates cwd but not the child's state root. 3. Reasonix's session import then picks that file up; since the probe's cwd belongs to no project, the conversation gets bound to the default workspace. Net effect: every "Test connection" click deposits a ghost conversation into the user's Reasonix app — one the user never created and can't attribute to OpenDesign. descriptions.github:5691531338: Every tweet is sent to the model each time it is seen. The service worker caches verdicts for the session, but the cache is lost when the browser restarts, so tweets that reappear later cost another API call. Idea: persist verdicts in chrome.storage.local , keyed by tweet ID plus a hash of the active filters, strictness and model settings, with an expiry and a size cap. Things to think about: - Invalidate when filters, threshold, model or provider change. - Keep the cache bounded so storage doesn't grow forever. - Don't cache failed calls. - Don't store more tweet text than needed. Storing only the verdict is enough. This is a bigger change than the other open issues. Please comment with your approach before starting. Where to look: the caching code in background.js and the decisions map in content.js .

descriptions.github:5690056464: Problem Each hub runs inference on a single CLAUDE CODE OAUTH TOKEN . When that token hits its usage limit, is revoked or expires, every hub that uses it stops answering. The only fix today is to rotate the token by hand and restart. Since 1.0.x people see a plain "usage limit" message ( hubzoid/agent errors.py ). That message should be the last resort, not the first thing that happens. Proposal - Accept an optional secondary token, for example CLAUDE CODE OAUTH TOKEN SECONDARY . - Switch to it on a usage limit or an authentication failure, and on N consecutive failures of the primary. - Switch back to the primary once its limit window resets. Log each switch and alert the admin once per window. - When both tokens are limited, show the existing plain message. Acceptance criteria - [ ] With one token configured, nothing changes. - [ ] A limited or rejected primary token sends the next…
descriptions.github:5690055984: Problem POST /api/auth/signup charges an attempt to the rate limit, then refunds it when the sign-up succeeds ( ratelimit.record success in hubzoid/auth/routes.py ). Every successful sign-up is free, so one address can create accounts without limit. In a reproduction, 11 sign-ups went through against a limit of 10. Proposal - Add a separate signup: counter in hubzoid/auth/ratelimit.py . It counts every sign-up and never refunds. - Check it before the existing per-address check. - Update the rate-limit section of docs/auth.md . Acceptance criteria - [ ] Write a failing test first: N+1 successful sign-ups from one address, where the last is refused with 429 . - [ ] Sign-in rate limiting is unchanged. A successful sign-in still clears the counter. - [ ] The docs are updated. A small, self-contained change, and a good first issue.

descriptions.github:5690035652: Before we start, are you using the latest version of Alicorn? Yes. (Please note that only the latest version is supported.) What feature do you want to land in Alicorn? Rewrites most infrastructure & GUI code in Rust for: - Enforcing better error handling, thus improving reliability. - Phasing out Electron for smaller binary size & memory footprint. In particular, this rewrite is NOT likely going to make any operation faster — Node.js is already performant for I/O intensive tasks like a launcher. This rewrite mainly wants to replace the "it works until it doesn't" philosophy with "check it or fail it". The only part that requires a web environment is OAuth login, which is temporary and is not likely to present when the game is running. A webview library, device code authorization, or asking the user to copy-paste callback URL will all be sufficient. Please tell us why it cannot be…

Ideas: - Pull fields out of a receipt or invoice into a dataclass - Label GitHub issues or PRs from their text - Clean up a messy CSV column, using thunc.map over the rows - Grade answers against a rubric, using ensure= to keep scores in range - Something from your own work Guidelines: - One file, runnable from the repo root as python3 -m examples. - Pick the backend with os.environ.get("THUNC BACKEND", "claude-code") , like the existing examples - A docstring at the top saying what it shows - Add a row to the Examples table in the README Comment with the example you're taking so two people don't build the same one.
descriptions.github:5689993370: call() 's typed overload takes returns: type[T] . Literal[...] (and X | None ) are special forms, not types, so mypy and Pyright fall through to the overload that returns Any . doesn't have this gap, because the return annotation is read from the function itself. Possible directions: - PEP 747 TypeForm , imported only under TYPE CHECKING , since thunc can't take a runtime dependency on typing extensions - Extra overloads for the common cases Requirements: any fix has to pass mypy --strict thunc and Pyright, and must not change runtime behaviour. A small file of reveal type / assert type checks would make the result easy to verify.
descriptions.github:5689993217: The OpenAI backend ( 5) reads OPENAI BASE URL , so it may already work with local model servers. Nobody has checked yet. Wanted: try it with one or more of Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio or llama.cpp's server, and report back here: - Which server, version and model - Does the backend connect? It uses the OpenAI Responses API, which not every local server implements. - Do the live tests pass? Run THUNC BACKEND=openai OPENAI BASE URL=... OPENAI API KEY=anything pytest live tests Possible outcomes: - It works: a short README section on running thunc locally. - It doesn't: a backend that uses Chat Completions instead, which more servers support. A comment with your results is useful even if you don't open a PR.
descriptions.github:5689993072: Right now every call goes to the model, so re-running a script costs the same every time, and tests that use a real model aren't reproducible. Wanted: - Cache: identical calls (same backend, model, system prompt and prompt text) return the stored answer. - Record/replay: record a run's answers, then replay them, for example in CI, failing loudly on any call that wasn't recorded. Open design questions (please discuss here before writing code): - How is it switched on? thunc.configure(cache="...") , an env var, a context manager? - Where does it store answers? A directory of JSON files is easy to diff and commit. - Should a cached answer still be parsed and ensure= -checked? Probably yes. - How does it interact with trace= ? Where: thunc/core.py ( send is the single point every call goes through) and thunc/config.py . It must stay standard-library only.
descriptions.github:5689992935: Allow a Pydantic model as a return type, next to dataclasses: Constraint: thunc's core uses the standard library only, so Pydantic must not become a dependency. Detect models by duck typing ( model json schema / model validate ) instead of importing Pydantic. Where: thunc/schema.py - describe() : describe the fields, possibly from model json schema() . - validate() : call model validate(value) and turn a ValidationError into a ValueError with a short message. That message is sent back to the model on retry. Tests: offline only, in tests/test schema.py . Pydantic can be a dev-only dependency, or the tests can skip when it isn't installed. Please comment with the approach before opening a large PR.
descriptions.github:5689992702: Allow an enum.Enum subclass as a return type, the same way Literal[...] works today: Where: thunc/schema.py - describe() : list the members' values, like the Literal branch does. - validate() : return tp(value) , and raise ValueError with the allowed values when it doesn't match, so the model gets a useful retry message. - parse() : accept an unquoted label, like the Literal near-miss handling. Tests: add cases to tests/test schema.py , and one end-to-end case with the fake backend fixture in tests/conftest.py . No real model is needed. Also add Enum to the return types list in the README.

descriptions.github:5689926426: Goal Create concise guides that let a contributor work on one JARVIS subsystem without reading the entire repository. Candidate guides - Realtime voice/audio - Windows automation - Gateway - Memory - Neural UI - Integrations/telephony Each guide should explain - Responsibility of the subsystem - Important files/modules - Interfaces with neighboring subsystems - How to run relevant tests - Common failure modes - Safe extension points Acceptance criteria Start with one subsystem and keep the guide verified against the current codebase.
descriptions.github:5689926064: Goal Make automated checks catch more of the failures that only appear on the supported Windows environment. Candidate areas - Python tests - Type checking - Ruff - Node/TypeScript checks - Gateway protocol tests - Windows integration smoke tests where practical Acceptance criteria - Keep CI reasonably fast - Clearly separate deterministic unit checks from environment-dependent tests - Document any tests that require a real Windows runner or optional services
descriptions.github:5689925468: Goal Audit structured logs and diagnostics for accidental exposure of secrets or private user data. Check - API keys and tokens - Cookies/session identifiers - Personal messages/transcripts - File contents and paths - Authorization payloads - Environment variables - Error objects containing credentials Acceptance criteria - Produce a short audit report - Fix confirmed leaks - Add redaction tests for sensitive fields - Preserve useful debugging information after redaction
descriptions.github:5689925280: Goal Improve the Memory Fabric so contributors can understand why a memory was retrieved and users receive more relevant context. Ideas - Better FTS5 query construction - Result ranking/weighting - Metadata filtering - Retrieval diagnostics - Tests for conflicting or stale memories Acceptance criteria - Retrieval behavior is measurable with representative test cases - Debug output can explain relevance without exposing private data - No cross-session memory leakage - Existing memory storage compatibility is preserved
descriptions.github:5689924386: Goal Make realtime Gemini Live sessions recover gracefully from transient connection failures. Investigate - WebSocket disconnects - Network interruptions - Session expiration - Audio stream recovery - Duplicate or lost events during reconnect Acceptance criteria - Reproduce at least one disconnect scenario - Retry with bounded backoff - Restore a consistent JARVIS session state - Avoid duplicate tool execution - Surface unrecoverable failures clearly - Add regression tests where feasible
descriptions.github:5689923436: Goal Improve the reliability of discovering Windows UI Automation elements before invoking actions. Investigate - ControlViewWalker traversal - Window targeting/focus - Element name/automation-id matching - Dynamic UIs and stale elements - Timeout and retry behavior Acceptance criteria - Reproduce at least one current discovery failure - Improve matching without relying on fragile coordinates as the primary path - Handle stale/invalid COM elements safely - Add regression coverage where practical
descriptions.github:5689923036: Goal Give users clear UI feedback when JARVIS loses a Gateway connection, model session, audio device, or other required subsystem. Acceptance criteria - Distinguish transient reconnecting state from permanent configuration failure - Provide actionable user-facing information - Prevent stale "thinking" or "speaking" states after disconnect - Recover automatically when the underlying service returns - Do not expose internal stack traces or secrets in the normal UI
descriptions.github:5689922828: Goal Improve the readability and smoothness of streamed assistant text and particle-based typography. Areas to investigate - Streaming text layout and line wrapping - Typography readability at different window sizes - Particle flight timing and cleanup - Long-response behavior - Text/voice synchronization Acceptance criteria - Long responses do not break the layout - No obvious memory/DOM growth during repeated turns - Animations degrade gracefully on lower-end hardware - Existing realtime behavior remains functional
descriptions.github:5689922653: Goal Improve the visual state machine for listening, thinking, searching, speaking, done, idle, and error states. Acceptance criteria - State transitions are visually distinct but not distracting - Transitions remain synchronized with actual Gateway events - No animation continues indefinitely after a terminal/error state - Interruption and reconnect flows are represented cleanly - Keep the implementation reusable rather than hard-coding state-specific UI in many components
descriptions.github:5689922434: Goal Create a first-class settings/diagnostics surface in the JARVIS desktop UI. Ideas - Show connection state for Gateway, model sessions, audio, and integrations - Surface configuration errors without exposing secrets - Provide basic runtime/version information - Show recent subsystem errors or health status - Make common configuration paths discoverable Acceptance criteria - Uses existing Gateway/state mechanisms where possible - Never displays API keys, tokens, cookies, or private session data - Works in both healthy and degraded states - Keeps the UI modular and consistent with the current design

descriptions.github:5689910199: Description Since PR 954 (issue 900), StreamedResponseStrategy stops sending after TcpConnection::send() returns false and destroys the connection. descriptions.github:5689899948: Goal Reduce the amount of time a new contributor spends fighting environment/setup problems. Ideas - Better startup validation - Dependency/version diagnostics - Clear missing-environment-variable errors - Useful subsystem health checks - More actionable Windows-specific error messages - A contributor-friendly diagnostic command - Documentation links in setup failures Acceptance criteria A developer who has a missing dependency, invalid configuration, unavailable service, or incompatible environment should get an actionable explanation instead of a low-level traceback alone.
descriptions.github:5689899647: Goal Increase regression coverage around the parts of JARVIS where failures are expensive or difficult to diagnose. descriptions.github:5689899431: Goal Make JARVIS easier for a new developer to understand, run, debug, and contribute to. Areas to improve - Development setup on Windows - Repository structure - Architecture entry points - Common development workflows - Debugging guides - Configuration/environment documentation - Feature-specific documentation - Examples for extending JARVIS - Troubleshooting common failures - Links between README, architecture docs, and subsystem manuals Acceptance criteria A new contributor should be able to: 1. Understand the major JARVIS subsystems 2. Set up the project locally 3. Find where a feature is implemented 4. Run relevant tests/checks 5. Understand where to ask for help or start contributing Prefer concrete examples and verified commands over generic prose.
descriptions.github:5689899052: Goal Perform a careful dead-code and unused-code audit across the repository. Format - DE followed by 9 digits; the first digit is never 0 . - Spaces or dots between groups are common ( DE ). - The 9th digit is a check digit (ISO 7064 MOD 11,10): product = 10 ; for each of the first 8 digits, sum = (digit + product) mod 10 , if sum == 0: sum = 10 , product = (2 sum) mod 11 . descriptions.github:5689427317: Problem Description In lib/state.js , writeJsonAtomic performs a write to a temporary file followed by fs.renameSync(temporaryPath, filePath) . On Windows, background file indexing services, antivirus scanners, or active IDE file watchers (like VS Code) can hold a transient read lock on filePath for a few milliseconds, occasionally causing fs.renameSync to throw an EPERM or EBUSY error. Expected Behavior Atomic writes should be resilient to momentary Windows file locks by attempting up to 3 retries with a small backoff before throwing. In frontend/index.html , "verifies citations" appears in: - the meta description (line 11) - the Open Graph description (line 30) - the Twitter description (line 39) - the JSON-LD description (line 54) - the keywords, as "citation verification" (line 12) The pipeline checks that citations resolve to papers in the corpus and that numbers match extracted evidence. It does not check that a source supports a sentence. What to do Reword these to what the code does, for example "checks that citations resolve to real papers" or "traces claims to source passages". Keep the descriptions concise and keep the keywords useful for search. Context: see the "Do not overclaim" rule in CONTRIBUTING.md .
descriptions.github:5687851396: ORCID author enrichment ( backend/app/tools/orcid search.py ) is limited in three ways: - it is opt-in ( ORCID AUTHOR ENRICHMENT=1 ), - it only covers the first 2 authors ( max authors=2 ), - it replaces the display name but does not store the ORCID iD. What to build Add an orcid field per author on PaperRecord (or a parallel list), store the iD when the match is confident, and render it in the reference list and exports where appropriate. Keep the confident-match rule so wrong iDs are never attached. Notes The extra lookups cost latency, so keep the feature opt-in and consider making max authors configurable. Tests must mock the ORCID API.
descriptions.github:5687851163: metadata validator agent ( backend/app/agents/research mode/retrieval.py ) normalises titles and strips blank author entries. Its docstring states that it does not validate venues, clean or resolve DOIs, or cross-check metadata against a registry. The name suggests more than it does. Pick one - Make it validate : normalise DOIs, optionally resolve them against Crossref or DataCite, and flag records whose title or year disagrees with the registry. - Rename it to something like metadata normalizer , and update the graph node, the UI stage label ("6. Metadata Validation" in frontend/app.js ), and the docs. Please comment which option you want before starting. Keep network calls out of the default test run.
descriptions.github:5687850934: evidence auditor agent ( backend/app/agents/research mode/synthesis.py ) is a graph step that only logs how many evidence records and papers enter synthesis. It performs no checks, but the name and its place in the graph suggest it does. Pick one - Make it useful : flag evidence records with no quote, no metric where one is expected, or whose paper is missing from the corpus, and report the counts in the state. - Remove it : delete the node from backend/app/graph/research mode builder.py and the exports in backend/app/agents/research mode/ init .py , and update the README agent count if it changes. Please say in a comment which option you are taking before you start. Tests must pass either way.
descriptions.github:5687850725: OpenAlex returns is retracted and Semantic Scholar returns isRetracted . Both are mentioned in the provider modules ( backend/app/tools/openalex search.py , backend/app/tools/semantic scholar search.py ), but the value is discarded when records are normalised, so a retracted paper can be cited in a generated paper with no warning. What to build - Add an is retracted field to PaperRecord (default False ). - Populate it from both providers. - Show a visible flag in the evidence corpus view and in the exported references, and exclude or warn at the screening gate. Tests Add provider unit tests with a mocked response where the flag is true (see tests/test provider adapters unit.py ).
descriptions.github:5687850514: A claim → evidence → paper chain is built only for sentences the writer LLM tagged with [EV: ] , and only in four sections. Whether a sentence gets tagged is up to the model, so untagged factual sentences get no chain and no check. What to build Report coverage and close the gap: 1. Compute and show the share of factual sentences that have a chain, per section. 2. Optionally flag untagged sentences that contain numbers, comparisons, or citations so the writer or the reviewer sees them. Notes - Tag instructions are in backend/app/agents/research mode/writing.py ; the tag-to-claim conversion is claims linker node . - Do not claim full coverage anywhere in the UI or docs. The goal is to make the gap visible first.
descriptions.github:5687850479: Add a small native example that reads an included public JSON fixture with read file, selects a value with json select, and checks an exact deterministic output rule. descriptions.github:5687850317: Claims are extracted per sentence. A sentence with two clauses and one citation counts as a single claim, so the second clause is never checked on its own. What to build Split compound sentences into clause-level claims before they are linked to evidence, for example on semicolons and coordinating conjunctions, while keeping the citation attached to the clause it belongs to. A simple rule-based splitter is fine as a first version. Notes - The claims manifest is built in claims linker node in backend/app/agents/research mode/writing.py . - Claim IDs are deterministic ( {section} cl001 ). Splitting must keep them stable and unique. - Add tests with multi-clause sentences, abbreviations ("et al.", "e.g."), and decimals, which must not trigger a split.
descriptions.github:5687850114: validate citations in text in backend/app/agents/research mode/validation.py resolves an in-text citation by matching only the first-author surname and the year against the corpus. Problem - Two papers by the same first author in the same year are indistinguishable. - Surnames with particles, hyphens, or diacritics (de la Cruz, Müller/Mueller) can fail to match. - A wrong citation that happens to share a surname and year counts as resolved. What to build A stricter match, for example adding the second author or title tokens when available, handling a / b year suffixes, and normalising diacritics. Keep the current behaviour as the fallback so existing reports do not regress. Acceptance - New unit tests cover same-author-same-year ambiguity, diacritics, and suffixes. - Existing validation tests still pass.
descriptions.github:5687849791: Research Mode confirms that a quoted passage exists in the cited paper. It does not test that the claim in the paper follows from that passage. Claim text is written by the LLM, and nothing compares it with the evidence quote. The model already has fields for this, hypothesis support and hypothesis relevance in backend/app/models/evidence.py , but nothing fills them. What to build A support check between a ReviewClaim and the EvidenceRecord it points at, for example an entailment prompt that returns supported / partial / unsupported with a short reason. Store the result on the claim and surface it in the validation report. Notes - Keep it separate from the existing resolution and numeric-match gates, which are deterministic. This check is model-based, so label the output as such and never call a result "verified". - Tests must run offline with a mocked LLM. - Please comment your…

descriptions.github:5687586722: Each parcel sensor carries a link back to Airmee's own tracking page, built from the token you entered. The format is taken from what Airmee's tracking site appears to use, not from a confirmed redirect. There is also a sign that the tracking site may have moved to a newer request shape than the one the integration calls. The current route still answers, so nothing is broken, but it is worth knowing which one is now canonical. What would help: compare the link on the parcel sensor with the link Airmee actually sent you. If they differ, the real one (with the token removed) would settle it.
descriptions.github:5687586450: Account mode logs in with an SMS code and then keeps itself signed in by refreshing its tokens. The whole flow — requesting the code, exchanging it, refreshing, and listing deliveries — was reconstructed from how the Airmee app behaves, and has never been run against the live service from here. Specifically unconfirmed: - The exact country code format accepted when requesting the SMS (what you type is sent as-is — +46 , 46 and 0046 have not been compared). - The shape of the refresh response, and whether both tokens really rotate. - The shape of the deliveries list. What would help: if setup fails or you get signed out unexpectedly, the warning line from the log plus a diagnostics export. The log line is written to be safe to paste.

descriptions.github:5687584257: The order object has several time fields for the delivery window. Their unit and timezone are unconfirmed, so the integration deliberately leaves planned from and planned to empty and does not claim the delivery window capability. sensor.airmee next delivery therefore stays unknown , and the Deliveries calendar has nothing to place. Timestamps are currently accepted only as Unix seconds in a plausible range; anything else is refused with a one-shot warning rather than guessed at. What would help: a diagnostics export from a parcel with a known delivery window. Comparing the raw numbers against what the Airmee app showed you settles the unit and timezone in one go, and then these fields can be switched on.
descriptions.github:5687583859: Airmee's order object carries its status in two places: a machine-readable code per timeline event, and a human-readable text field. The integration prefers the code, and only falls back to mapping the text when the code is absent — the text is localized and ambiguous, so the fallback deliberately maps only unmistakable wordings. Which of the two the tracking-link route actually returns has never been seen on a real response. The account route is expected to carry both. What would help: if you track a real parcel by tracking link, a diagnostics export would show whether the per-event status code comes through. If it only ever returns the text, the fallback map needs widening and this gets reprioritised.

descriptions.github:5687540452: The Structural Health Monitoring section has six entries and all of them are modal analysis tools (operational or experimental modal analysis and camera based displacement measurement). The section note already says it is thin. The concrete gaps are: - Damage detection and anomaly detection on vibration or strain data. - Sensor data pipelines : acquisition, cleaning and storage of long term monitoring data. - Benchmark datasets from instrumented bridges or buildings, which would also fit Open Datasets. - Fatigue and remaining life assessment tools. Projects must meet the usual criteria: open source license, documentation and either active maintenance or a clear reason to list them anyway. Suggestions as comments or pull requests are welcome.
descriptions.github:5687540276: Crack and surface defect detection is one of the most common uses of machine learning in civil engineering, and the AI and Machine Learning section currently has no project for it. The two entries that used to cover it, DeepCrack and crack segmentation, were removed in 10 because neither repository has a license, and DeepCrack restricts its data to non commercial use. SDNET2018 in Open Datasets provides images, but there is no listed model or training code. What is needed A project for crack or defect segmentation or detection on concrete, asphalt or steel surfaces that: - has an explicit open source license for the code, - states the license or terms of any bundled dataset or weights, - documents how to run inference or training. Suggestions as comments or pull requests are welcome.
descriptions.github:5687540106: The Learning Resources section covers GIS, geotechnical engineering, hydraulics and general engineering computation, but has nothing for three areas the list itself is strong in: - Earthquake engineering : course notes or worked notebooks on response spectra, ground motion processing, hazard or nonlinear time history analysis. - Structural dynamics : open textbooks or notebooks on single and multi degree of freedom systems and modal analysis. - BIM and IFC : tutorials for IfcOpenShell, openBIM workflows or IFC data handling. Candidates that were looked at and rejected because the repository has no license: the DOLFINx tutorial and seismo-live. A resource needs an explicit open license (code or content, for example MIT or CC BY) and enough documentation to follow without the lecture it was written for. Suggestions as comments or pull requests are welcome.

descriptions.github:5686950837: Summary parse file crashes with an unhandled UnicodeDecodeError when a non-Cursor log file is UTF-16 encoded. CursorParser survives this (it retries through ("utf-8", "utf-16", "latin-1") ), but ClaudeCodeParser , CodexParser , OpenCodeParser and HermesParser all open with the default UTF-8 and let the decode error escape. Because parse all logs calls parse file in a loop over every .jsonl / .json / .log under a --path directory, a single UTF-16 file in the tree aborts the whole run — so one unparseable file takes out every other log in the same invocation. Found while reviewing 179; reproduced on main at a276c20 , so it predates that work and is not a regression from it. descriptions.github:5685537359: Public-mode keys are shared today in person, as a pairing text or a QR code (spec section 9). That works between people who meet, but an organisation (a bank, a newsroom, a public figure) needs a way for anyone to find its key. The spec marks this TBD . Candidates to compare: - A well-known HTTPS path on the organisation's domain ( /.well-known/voxtrust ), like security.txt . - A DNS TXT record, possibly with DNSSEC. - Key transparency logs, so a swapped key is visible. - Reusing an existing system (C2PA trust lists, WebFinger, Keybase-style proofs). What matters: a verifier must be able to tell a key that rotated legitimately from one an attacker swapped, and the answer must work offline after the first lookup. Comments with prior art and trade-offs are very welcome before any spec text is written.
descriptions.github:5685536907: C2PA Content Credentials are becoming the standard for signed media provenance. File mode is close to it in spirit (a signed manifest inside the file), and a bridge would let C2PA-aware tools show a Vox Trust seal (roadmap, phase 6). Open questions, a design note answering them is a great first contribution: - Should the VOXT manifest become a custom C2PA assertion, or should Vox Trust per-chunk digests map onto C2PA's existing hashing of media? - C2PA signs with X.509 certificates; Vox Trust uses bare Ed25519 keys pinned by contacts. How do the two trust models coexist? - What does a verifier show when the C2PA signature and the Vox Trust seal disagree? Prototype with the c2pa Rust crate. Please start with a short design note (a markdown file in docs/decisions/ ) before a large PR.

descriptions.github:5685536145: The core already implements the pairing text of spec section 9 ( vox trust core::pairing , with encode and decode ), but the command-line tool cannot produce or read one. Today you share a public key as 64 hex characters. Proposal: - vox-trust pubkey KEYFILE --pairing [LABEL] prints voxtrust:0:public: < 64 hex [: ] . - vox-trust verify FILE --pin also accepts a pairing text (or a file containing one) besides a bare hex key. - Circle pairing texts contain the secret, so the CLI must never print one unless asked explicitly, and the help text should say why. Where: crates/vox-trust-cli/src/main.rs (argument parsing and the USAGE text), tests in crates/vox-trust-cli/tests/ . Keep the existing exit codes. A CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased] is welcome.
descriptions.github:5685535666: Vox Trust is meant to be built into apps that already record or send voice: messengers, voicemail, podcast and newsroom tools, support platforms. If you tried it ( npm install vox-trust , cargo add vox-trust-core , or the CLI), comment here with: - what kind of app, and which platform (browser, Node, Rust, mobile) - where you got stuck, or what took longer than it should - whether your upload path kept the file bit-exact (file mode needs that) - what API you wished existed A short comment is enough. descriptions.github:5685535295: Only the author has reviewed the design and the code. Before anyone relies on it, it needs eyes from people who break protocols for a living. Scope, most valuable first: 1. Threat model: attackers or attacks that are missing, and claims that are too strong. 2. File mode (spec section 6): domain separation, what the signature covers and what it does not ( byte rate , extra chunks, chunk order), replay, downgrade between circle and public mode. 3. crates/vox-trust-core (about 2 000 lines, no unsafe ): the WAV parser and the manifest decoding. 4. crates/vox-trust-cli/src/keyfile.rs : Argon2id parameters and XChaCha20-Poly1305 usage. Findings that could hurt users go through private vulnerability reporting (SECURITY.md); everything else as issues. Reviewers will be credited in the changelog and the threat model.
descriptions.github:5685534877: The specification becomes 1.0 only after a second implementation, written by someone other than the author, agrees with the reference on every test vector (roadmap). descriptions.github:5684982544: Summary With hooks.transparent prefixes = ["sudo", "sudo -E"] , rtk discover counts sudo RTK DISABLED=1 docker ps and RTK DISABLED=1 sudo docker ps as bypasses ( 3808), but not the same lines with an expanded value: rtk rewrite "sudo docker ps" rewrites under that config, so dropping the assignment would recover the savings. Cause strip disabled prefix for analytics ( src/discover/registry.rs ) walks raw lexer::tokenize tokens, which split one shell word at $ : RTK DISABLED=$CI is two tokens, RTK DISABLED= and $CI . The walk treats $CI as the command word, finds it unsupported, and falls back to strip disabled prefix , which does not peel sudo . Walking coalesced words ( lexer::coalesce words , as without rtk disabled in src/discover/mod.rs does) would keep the assignment whole. A missed count, not a wrong one: develop does not count these lines either. Related: 3756, 3808.

descriptions.github:5684767719: Context BrowserRemoteTransport ( src/browser.ts lines 237-327): 1. flush() (line 275) only treats a thrown fetch as failure. A 500 or 413 response resolves normally, so those entries are dropped without any signal. 2. On network failure the batch is put back with this.batch.unshift(...entries) (line 290) with no upper bound. If the endpoint is down for an hour, the buffer grows without limit in the user's tab. 3. descriptions.github:5684431226: Problem When a human files a bug, the hive withholds the closing keyword from the fix PR: validatePRRequestClaims rewrites Closes N to Refs N unless the issue already has hive: reporter-confirmed ( humanFiledBugReason / IsHumanFiledBugReport in src/pkg/github/pr request claims.go , from kubestellar/hive 6781). The fix PR merges and the issue stays open until the reporter confirms the fix with /fixed or the label. That gate makes sense when the reporter saw a symptom and can check whether it went away (the 6500 → 6762/ 6767 case). It works badly for two common kinds of human-filed bugs: 1. Code-sweep findings. A maintainer or contributor reviews a subsystem and files a batch of defects found by reading the code: races, lossy keys, unbounded reads, doc/code drift, tests that don't test the real contract. There's no symptom the reporter observed, so "reporter confirms the symptom is gone"…

descriptions.github:5684207567: What is wrong No handler or middleware limits the request body size. json.NewDecoder(r.Body) reads whatever arrives. With auth on and --bind 0.0.0.0 , an authenticated client can make the server buffer an arbitrarily large body. What we want Add http.MaxBytesReader in the middleware chain that already wraps every route. 1 MiB is far more than any request body the API takes. An oversized body answers 413 as problem+json through respondError . Where to look - src/internal/httpapi/middleware.go and src/internal/httpapi/server.go - src/internal/httpapi/problems.go and docs/adr/0006-api-conventions.md for the error shape - The api-change skill / API docs: any new status code must be listed in the API reference Definition of done - [ ] A body over the limit gets 413 problem+json; a body just under it is accepted. - [ ] The limit applies to every /api/v2 route with a body (table-driven test…
descriptions.github:5684207074: What is wrong run.( Engine).Submit checks ActiveRunForLock and then calls CreateRun as two separate statements. The index on runs.lock key is not unique, so two submits that land between those calls both succeed. That can happen with two UI requests, or the CLI in one terminal and the UI in another. Two runs then hold one lock, which is exactly what ADR-0004 exists to prevent. What we want Make the check and the insert one atomic statement, so it also holds across processes: Report zero rows affected as the LockConflictError . The alternative is a partial unique index on lock key WHERE status IN (…) AND lock key != '' , which needs a migration. Where to look - src/internal/run/engine.go ( Submit ) - src/internal/store/runs.go ( CreateRun , ActiveRunForLock ) - src/internal/store/migrations/ if you take the index route Definition of done - [ ] A test submits the same lock key…
descriptions.github:5684206511: What is wrong labctl never installs a signal handler, so cmd.Context() is context.Background() and Ctrl-C kills the process with Go's default action. Scripts started through internal/toolchain run in their own process group ( Setpgid ), so the terminal's SIGINT does not reach them. They keep running with no parent, and their run stays running until the next engine start reconciles it. That breaks the promise in ADR-0003. Two smaller effects of the same gap: - labctl ui exits without calling Shutdown on the HTTP server. - scenario verify --watch sleeps with time.Sleep , which no context can interrupt. What we want - In cli.Execute , run the root command under signal.NotifyContext(ctx, os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM) via rootCmd.ExecuteContext . Everything already reads cmd.Context() , so cancellation flows to run.Engine and each process group gets its graceful SIGTERM. - labctl ui calls…
descriptions.github:5684205957: What is wrong Engine.Get returns the Scenario held in the engine's cache, but only after setting s.Active on it. Any two goroutines that call Get at the same time, or one that calls Get while a run reads the scenario, race on that field. - go test -race ./internal/service/scenario/ reports it on main in TestActivate ConflictsPerScenario , which fails most runs. - The race is also live in labctl ui , because its HTTP handlers call Get concurrently. What we want Stop writing to the cached value. Return a shallow copy with Active filled in, so every caller stays the same. (Dropping the field in favour of IsActive(name) is the alternative, but it touches every caller; take the copy approach first.) Where to look - src/internal/scenario/engine.go ( Get , isActive ) - src/internal/service/scenario/ for the failing test Definition of done - [ ] Get never mutates the cached scenario. - [ ] A…
descriptions.github:5684205515: What is wrong Engine.Down prints an uninstall error as a warning, carries on, removes the .active marker and returns success. On a lab whose API server was timing out, scenario down event-driven-arch and scenario down gitops-cicd both reported succeeded while every kubectl delete failed with TLS handshake timeout . Producers, consumers, the ArgoCD Applications, namespaces, ServiceMonitors and dashboard ConfigMaps were all left running. Because the marker was gone, scenario down then refused with "not active", so the only way out was deleting by hand. scenarios/gitops-cicd/scripts/remove-apps.sh makes it worse: it prints ✓ gitops-demo and gitops-broken removed after its own deletes failed, because every command ends in || true . What we want 1. Down collects uninstall errors. When any component fails it keeps the marker, names the failed components, and returns an error telling the user…

descriptions.github:5684142179: Problem A: In Admin → Users → "Change pw", leaving the field empty and pressing Save sends the request. The server silently ignores an empty password ( if (password) ), but the UI closes the editor as if it had been saved. Problem B: If creating a user fails, the message is shown as Error: Username already taken — with the "Error:" prefix ( String(createMut.error) ). Other pages (Wrapped, Discover) strip the prefix. Where: web/src/pages/admin/UsersPage.tsx What to do: (A) disable Save while the password field is empty (or don't submit). (B) strip the prefix or use error.message . Acceptance criteria - [ ] Two new tests in UsersPage.test.tsx : Save is disabled / no request for an empty password; the error message is shown without the prefix.
descriptions.github:5684141991: A few actions swallow errors and show nothing, so the user presses a button and nothing seems to happen. Don't change the existing behaviour (optimistic revert etc.). descriptions.github:5683511344: Problem or use case There is no omni command that closes or deletes a session. The API supports it ( DELETE /v1/sessions/{id} ), and the web UI can archive. From a terminal, the closest is omni host stop-session . That stops the runner but leaves the session in the list. A script or a user cleaning up test or probe sessions must call the HTTP API by hand, with a bearer token. Proposed solution omni session close ... (archive) and omni session delete ... (with a confirm, or --yes ). Both should take --server and use the same auth as omni session export . Alternatives considered curl -X DELETE with a token from the server's auth flow. It works, but it is undiscoverable and makes users handle tokens themselves. Related: 4834 and 7498 (the agent-side sys session close gaps).

descriptions.github:5683459075: Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. Describe the solution you'd like I'd like all FreeRTOS object deletion APIs to automatically clear any granted ACL permissions to the surviving tasks. descriptions.github:5681561743: Why The Appearance dialog draws clickable controls, but its keyboard handling currently only supports Escape. Scope Add a visible focus indicator and Tab/Shift+Tab traversal for existing controls. Enter/Space activates the focused action; Escape closes and restores composer focus. Reuse the current appearance actions and limits; this does not depend on a separate disabled-button change. Done when - Theme, text size, UI scale, reading width, Reset, and Done are reachable without a mouse. - Focus remains within the dialog and cannot trigger underlying send/navigation actions. - Values still clamp at existing limits; clicks and keys agree even if all adjustment controls remain present. - Focus is visible in both themes, survives redraw/resize, and never changes the composer draft. Starting points controls, appearance actions, settings keyboard branch.
descriptions.github:5681560876: Why The header/footer show a project basename, which is ambiguous when two folders have the same name and cannot be copied directly. Scope Add a clearly labelled Copy path control next to the header project breadcrumb. Copy the complete current canonical project path using the existing SDL clipboard pattern. Do not change the active folder or add a new global shortcut. Done when - Same-basename projects copy their distinct full paths. - Spaces, Unicode, and long paths copy without the display label's truncation. - During a pending chat switch, copy the project shown by the breadcrumb. - Clipboard failure is reported; clicking does not alter the draft, caret, or chat selection. Starting points displayed project breadcrumb, clipboard pattern.
descriptions.github:5681560437: Why Clearing a library query currently requires editing the text; there is no clear control. Scope Show a clear button inside the query field only when the query is nonempty. Clear via the existing editor/request flow, reset paging, and keep the same scope and modal open. Reuse the existing action/target system. Done when - Clicking clears the query, returns to the first page, and keeps input focus. - A prior in-flight query cannot replace the new empty-query results. - The button never edits the chat draft or activates a selected result. - Empty queries hide the control; IME composition is cancelled cleanly before clearing. Starting points library actions, query field, query drawing.
descriptions.github:5681559956: Why The chat library uses the same No matches status for an empty workspace, empty archives, and a query with no results. Scope Show scope-specific guidance after a completed search. Distinguish an empty query from a nonempty query with no matches. Use existing scope/query/page state; do not add a new search or enrollment path. Done when - Empty Search explains creating/importing a chat; empty Archives explains archiving. - Empty Import Pi explains that there are no importable results in configured Pi storage, without claiming no sessions exist. - A nonempty query says no matches and suggests changing/clearing it. - Searching, indexing, incomplete sources, and errors retain their status rather than being mislabeled as empty. Starting points library scope and status.
descriptions.github:5681559500: Why Text size, scale, and reading width already clamp their values, but their minus/plus buttons still look and behave as enabled at the limits. Scope Render the exhausted direction as disabled and omit its hit target. Keep existing limits: text 12–24 px, UI scale 75–175%, and width 560–1120 px. Reuse the palette and existing adjustment actions. Done when - Each minimum disables only minus; each maximum disables only plus. - Disabled clicks do not change values, enqueue saves, or invalidate layouts. - Moving back into range re-enables the button; Reset restores the normal state. - Disabled controls remain recognizable in dark and light themes. Starting points value clamps, adjustment drawing.
descriptions.github:5681559176: Why The thinking menu supports mouse selection and Escape only; unlike the model picker, arrows and Enter cannot choose a level. Scope Highlight the current thinking level on opening. Up/Down move within Pi's supplied levels, Enter invokes the existing selection action, and Escape cancels. Use Pi's list rather than hardcoded levels. Done when - Keyboard and mouse choose the same level and close the menu. - Arrow movement clamps at the ends; an empty or refreshed list cannot submit a stale index. - Escape does not change the level or composer text. - The highlighted row is visible and distinguishable in both themes. Starting points thinking overlay, existing action, keyboard branch.
descriptions.github:5681558836: Why Shortcuts are implemented and listed in CLI help, but there is no in-app reference. Scope Add a Shortcuts entry in the sidebar opening a read-only help dialog. List existing navigation, sending, stop, search, model, settings, and zoom controls; show Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. Reuse the appearance dialog's drawing/modal conventions. Done when - Listed shortcuts match the current handlers; no new shortcuts are invented. - Escape/Close restores the previous composer draft, selection, and focus. - Typing while open never edits or sends the draft. - The list is readable at minimum window size, in both themes, and at 75%/175% UI scale. descriptions.github:5681551856: 赏金平台 / Platform GitHub 原始链接 / Source URL 漏洞描述 / Description [Bounty $1,000] FP32 ttnn.cumsum returns NaN after infinity or overflow 📝 Background ttnn.cumsum has a regression in its compensated FP32 accumulation path. After the running total becomes +inf or -inf—either because an input contains an infinity or because the sum overflows—subsequent output elements become NaN. This behavior diverges from PyTorch: Input: [1.0, inf, 1.0, 1.0] ttnn: [1.0, inf, nan, nan] torch: [1.0, inf, inf, inf] The regression was introduced by the compensated-summation change in 56811. The compensation calculation performs inf - inf, producing NaN; subsequent scan elements are then poisoned. The issue affects the default FP32 path. The existing disable compensated sum=True path avoids the failure but is deprecated and is not an acceptable long-term workaround. 🎯 What Success Looks Like The bounty is complete…

descriptions.github:5681232002: 🤖 This issue was found and written with AI (Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5). Problem --clear-session doesn't actually clear the session. In main.py the browser context is created first, and aenter loads storage state.json into it. Only after that does session.clear session() delete the file: The run still uses the old cookies, and aexit writes them back to disk. So the flag is a no-op. Fix - Delete the file before creating the context, e.g. by passing a fresh=True option to BrowserSession or by deleting it in main.py before the async with . - Alternatively, call context.clear cookies() like --form-login does. - Add a test asserting the context is created with storage state=None when --clear-session is given.

descriptions.github:5681088245: Summary codeprism visualize has no tests ( cli.py lines are uncovered). It writes a self-contained HTML graph, so a regression could ship a broken or empty file without any test failing. What to test Index a small project in tmp path (as tests/test cli.py does), then run visualize --out with CliRunner : - exit code 0, the output file exists and contains or quotes does not break the page (it is embedded in a script tag); - the default output name graph.html is used when --out is omitted (run inside tmp path ). Note: visualize /no/such/dir currently writes an empty graph.html and exits 0. That behaviour is tracked in 47, so please do not assert on it. How to check coverage Lines should become covered. Good first issue notes Test-only change. Run pytest and ruff check before opening the PR.

Start with FileEventHandler. accepts : unit-test it directly with a handful of paths; it needs no filesystem events. How to check coverage…
descriptions.github:5681087603: Summary codeprism scan . --diff validates the range with SAFE GIT REF RE , which allows a leading - . A value such as --stat , -p or --shortstat is therefore passed to git diff --name-only as an option, and the scan reports "No changed files" and exits 0. In a CI gate, a bad value passes silently instead of failing. (Git rejects branch names starting with - , so this is a hardening gap rather than an easy exploit, but the check exists specifically to keep git arguments safe.) Steps to reproduce Uses a throwaway git repository. Actual behaviour SAFE GIT REF RE = r"^[\w./ ^@{}:+\-]{1,200}$" ( codeprism/cli.py ) matches --stat , -p and --help . Expected behaviour A range starting with - is rejected with the existing "Invalid diff range" message and exit 1. Suggested fix - Require the first character not to be - , for example ^(?!-)[\w./ ^@{}:+\-]{1,200}$ . - Also pass --end-of-options (or…

descriptions.github:5680992241: GroqClient.SystemPrompt hard-codes English: The model handles many languages perfectly well. The only reason the review is English-only is that the prompt says so. What to build The flag should substitute the target language into the prompt and translate the section headings to match, so the output reads naturally rather than as translated English headings over a non-English body. Why it matters This project was built for the developer with no team to ask. That developer is not necessarily an English speaker, and a review you have to translate before you can act on it is a review you will skip. Notes - Default stays English, so nothing changes for existing users. - Accept ISO 639-1 codes ( pt , es , fr , de , ja ) and fall back to English with a warning on stderr for anything unrecognised. - Nothing parses the section names, so they are free to translate.
descriptions.github:5680986143: The CLI reviews local changes ( git diff , --staged , --diff ). It cannot review a pull request that is not checked out locally. What to build GitHub serves the raw diff for any PR at .diff , so this can be a plain HTTP GET followed by the existing review path — no API client, and no authentication needed for public repositories. Why it matters It turns the tool from "review what I am about to commit" into "review what someone sent me", which is the other half of reviewing alone: the maintainer triaging a drive-by contribution with nobody to ask for a second opinion. Notes - Private repositories need a token; treat that as a follow-up, not part of this. - Large PRs will hit the existing 60k-character truncation. That is fine, but the warning should name the PR that was truncated. - Parsing the URL belongs in CliOptions ; fetching belongs in its own small type next to GitDiff .

So a client cannot display "this will cost approximately X" before the user commits. The user sees only…

descriptions.github:5680947372: Problem Scripts/Info.plist still has CFBundleShortVersionString = 0.1.0 . - The release commit 0f1f26b chore(release): 0.2.0-beta.1 only changed CHANGELOG.md . - Scripts/build-app.sh:79-81 injects the version only when VERSION is set, and only release.yml sets it. - make-dmg.sh:12-13 takes the DMG name from this plist. descriptions.github:5680945971: Problem .github/workflows/ci.yml:42 : the build-and-test job runs make app . With the default VOICE HELPER=auto , that also builds the MLX voice helper, and without any package cache. The separate voice-helper job then builds the same helper again. In run , "Build app bundle" took about 6.5 minutes, and the voice-helper job took about 8 minutes on top of that. Suggested fix - Use VOICE HELPER=0 make app in build-and-test . The voice-helper job already covers the helper. - Add an actions/cache for .build , keyed on Package.resolved and the sources.

descriptions.github:5680944631: Problem Sources/MomoApp/Character/CharacterController.swift:18-41 keeps these settings only as plain properties with default values: - mood - brain - isLifeEnabled - isVisible The status menu changes them ( StatusMenu.swift:49-66 ), but none of them is stored in Preferences ( Support/AppSettings.swift:36-96 ). Scenario The user chooses "Hide Momo" or turns off "Live on Its Own". After a restart or the next login, Momo is back in the notch and animating, so the user has to change it again every session. Suggested fix - Add showsCharacter , isLifeEnabled , mood and brainSource to Preferences . - Apply them in AppModel.applyPreferences() , the same way characterID already is.
descriptions.github:5680944130: Problem None of the %lld keys in Sources/MomoApp/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings has plural variations. Examples: - "Starts in %lld minutes." - "%lld steps" - "Repeats every %lld days" - "You have %lld tasks due and %lld events today…" Scenario A meeting one minute away triggers "Starts in 1 minutes." ( ContextMonitor.swift:79 ). The morning greeting says "You have 1 tasks due and 1 events today." A count of 1 is the most common case. Suggested fix - Add en plural variations (one/other) for these keys in the String Catalog. - Make Scripts/check-localizations.py flag %lld keys that have no plural variations.
descriptions.github:5680943651: Problem Sources/MomoApp/Settings/BrainSettingsView.swift:152-155 : The switch has no accessibility label. The arrow buttons next to it are labelled just "Move up" / "Move down" ( :143, :150 ), without the brain's name. Scenario VoiceOver reads every row's switch as "switch, on". A blind user can't tell which brain they're about to turn off or reorder. Suggested fix - Use Toggle(BrainDescriptor.name(id), isOn: isEnabled).labelsHidden() , or add .accessibilityLabel(...) . - Include the brain's name in the arrow labels, for example String(format: L("Move %@ up"), name) .
descriptions.github:5680942615: Problem Sources/MomoApp/Context/ContextMonitor.swift:29 declares notificationsReady = false . It is set only once, at launch, in prepareNotifications() ( :210-215 ). Both notify ( :222 ) and scheduleReminderNotifications ( :247 ) start with guard canNotify, notificationsReady else { return } . Scenario The user declines the first-launch notification prompt, then later enables Momo in System Settings → Notifications. Until Momo is relaunched, all of these are silently dropped: - Task reminders - Routine replies - "Needs your answer" prompts - Meeting-note offers - The morning greeting A routine waiting on a consent prompt hangs with no signal at all. Suggested fix - Check UNUserNotificationCenter.current().notificationSettings().authorizationStatus before posting, or re-check on NSApplication.didBecomeActiveNotification . - Consider listing Notifications in the Permissions pane.
descriptions.github:5680942128: Problem Sources/MomoApp/Support/KeychainStore.swift:25-39 : setKey first calls SecItemDelete , then return SecItemAdd(...) == errSecSuccess . The method is marked , and every caller ignores the result: - Settings/AI/APIKeySetupView.swift:148 (sets result = .valid right after) - Settings/BrainSettingsView.swift:282 - Settings/ConnectionsSettingsView.swift:125 Scenario The user replaces a working key. SecItemAdd fails (the keychain is locked or access is denied). By then the old key has already been deleted and the new one wasn't saved, yet the UI shows "valid / connected". The next chat fails with an authentication error, far from the real cause. Suggested fix - Update the item with SecItemUpdate , falling back to SecItemAdd , so the old key is never deleted first. - Check the result at each call site (or make setKey throw the OSStatus ) and show an error instead of .valid .
descriptions.github:5680936876: Problem Sources/MomoMCP/MCPClient.swift:56-70 : LineBuffer.append keeps appending data until it sees \n , with no size limit. Both ProcessTransport and UnixSocketTransport use it. The server side already caps its buffer at 16 MB ( MCPSocketServer.swift:191 ); the client side has no cap. Scenario A buggy third-party MCP server streams a huge response, or endless output without a newline. Momo's memory grows until macOS kills the app. Suggested fix - Cap LineBuffer at 16 MB, matching the server. - On overflow, finish the stream with an error and close the transport.
descriptions.github:5680936294: Problem Sources/MomoApp/Context/MCPConnections.swift:66-77 starts the server process with ProcessTransport . If client.connect() throws (for example ClientError.timedOut after the fixed 30 s in MCPClient.swift:149 ) or listTools() throws, the catch block only sets .failed . It never calls client.close() , which is the only path that terminates the process ( MCPClient.swift:49-52 ). clients[id] stays nil , so the next refresh() starts yet another process. Scenario A server configured as npx -y some-server takes more than 30 s to install on first run. Momo marks it failed, but the node process keeps running. Every settings change or refresh adds another orphaned process. Suggested fix - Call await client.close() (or terminate the transport) in the catch . - Make the initialize timeout longer than, or separate from, the per-call timeout.

descriptions.github:5680934659: Problem Sources/MomoBrain/Providers/CommandLineTool.swift:151 : The .uncaughtSignal case is there for Momo's own terminate() on cancel. It also treats crashes as success: SIGSEGV, SIGABRT, and SIGKILL from the OS (for example an out-of-memory kill). Scenario codex or gemini crashes in the middle of an answer. The stream ends normally, and the user gets a partial or empty reply with no error. Suggested fix - Set a cancelledByUs flag in onTermination , and treat only that case as a clean finish. - For any other signal, finish with a failure that names the signal.

descriptions.github:5680932794: Problem The HTTP layer gives up on the first error, even when the error is temporary. - Sources/MomoBrain/HTTP.swift:28-37 throws on the first non-2xx response. - For 429 (rate limit), HTTP.swift:79-82 only changes the error wording. Retry-After is ignored, and Anthropic's 529 "overloaded" is reported as a generic 5xx. - Each tool round is a separate request ( AnthropicProvider.swift:64-108 ), so one temporary error ends a reply that may already be several steps in. Scenario A multi-step task completes 5 tool rounds, which have already taken real actions such as creating reminders. Round 6 gets a 529, and the whole reply fails. If the user clicks "Try again", the tools run again (see the retry/history issue). Suggested fix - In HTTP.streamLines , retry before any bytes have been yielded on 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 and 529. - Make 2–3 attempts with exponential backoff and jitter…

What the code does: - The classification request carries the repository, the issue title, the issue body and the repository's label set. The issue's current labels are not part of it. - The assign labels tool schema accepts any number of labels from the label set, and the system prompt has no rule such as "at most one type label and one priority label". - The selected labels are applied with POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n}/labels , which adds to whatever is already on the issue. GIFs have no audio, so leave out the opus flags. Keep Arg::VideoChain(&TRANSCODE CHAIN) so --fps and --resize still work, and register it next to the gif - mp4 line in insert media family . The "looping GIF becomes a single play" warning applies here too. One thing to check: GIFs can have transparent pixels, and VP9 webm can carry alpha ( -pix fmt yuva420p ). If that works, keep it. If not, add a warning saying transparency is lost. Done when conv in.gif out.webm works, the recipe snapshot has the new line, and the pair count at the top of the README is updated. descriptions.github:5680599426: Description cli/README.md documents that the rendered page goes to stdout ( :98 , :105 ), but it says nothing about the two other user-visible contracts of the binary: 1. Diagnostics go to stderr. Since 540 (PR 553) every runtime error message — missing argument, usage, URL parse, request creation, fetch failure, missing Edge-control header, response read failure, HTTP status = 400, unreadable input file — is written to os.Stderr . Exit codes. Since 460 (PR 539) every runtime error path exits 1 ; success exits 0. descriptions.github:5680591943: Description cli/mesi-cli.go never closes the HTTP response body. In URL mode the body is fetched at client.Do(req) ( cli/mesi-cli.go:306 ) and read with io.ReadAll(content.Body) ( cli/mesi-cli.go:317 ), but there is no defer content.Body.Close() anywhere, so the http.Response is dropped unread on every path that leaves the URL branch. Impact today is small but real: - the body is read to EOF on the success path, so the connection is handed back to the pool anyway and main returns immediately afterwards; - on every error branch os.Exit(1) is called, and os.Exit runs no deferred functions, so a defer content.Body.Close() placed at the top of the branch would not fire there either — the fds are only reclaimed when the process dies. So no leak is observable from the CLI as it is used today. The defect is the missing Close() itself: it is invisible only because the process is short-lived…
