Scope Add a checked-in JSON Schema for the version 1 envelope and failure records, plus a short pointer from the JSON documentation. Keep runtime dependencies unchanged. Acceptance criteria - Specify required properties, data types, schema version, and the actual supported kind values. - Define whether unknown fields are accepted, explaining the compatibility tradeoff rather than assuming one. - Include representative empty and non-empty valid examples and an…
descriptions.github:5680539876: Why this is useful Many reports put the same short exception text in the message attribute and at the start of the detail body. The current renderer shows both, which can spend a meaningful share of a small context budget on repeated information. A conservative presentation rule could improve readability, but fuzzy similarity or broad prefix deletion might remove an important distinction in an assertion. Scope Evaluate an opt-in Markdown-only rule for exact duplicated message lines after sanitization. Preserve the original structured fields and avoid changing parser deduplication. Acceptance criteria - Provide synthetic examples for an exact first-line duplicate, a near match, and a genuinely repeated diagnostic line. - Define treatment of whitespace and omission notices; do not accidentally compare truncated text as full evidence. - Keep differing messages and details intact and…
descriptions.github:5680539332: Why this is useful The Markdown header currently reports one total for all unique failure records. With many suites, a reader must scan the individual blocks to understand where failures cluster. A small per-suite summary could help prioritize investigation, particularly when the output budget omits later details. It must clearly summarize extracted unique records rather than claiming to reproduce original runner counters or the total number of executed tests. Scope Discuss an optional summary grouped by the suite identity already available in Failure. Do not change parsing, suite ancestry, deduplication, or failure selection. Acceptance criteria - Include a synthetic report with repeated suite names across reports and define the grouping key explicitly. - Ensure totals agree with the complete extracted failure set, including records whose details are omitted. - Bound summary size and…
descriptions.github:5680538872: Why this is useful The renderer deliberately keeps an ordered prefix of complete failure blocks. If the first block is too large, a brief may contain only the total and an omission notice even when later failures have useful short descriptions. Some workflows would benefit from seeing every selected test identity before allocating remaining space to details. This would be an alternative presentation strategy, not a parser-order change or a new failure filter. Scope Prototype an opt-in summary-first renderer that budgets concise identities before adding detailed blocks. Keep the current ordered-prefix strategy available. Acceptance criteria - Compare both strategies on a synthetic report with one large failure followed by several small failures. - Specify deterministic allocation and tie-breaking without implying all failure details were retained. - Count every summary, heading, and…
descriptions.github:5680538142: Why this is useful Character slicing uses Python code points, which is the documented budget unit, but a visible character can contain several code points. An excerpt boundary can separate an accent from its letter or split a joined emoji in a test message. This is mainly a readability issue and does not justify changing the tool into a tokenizer or silently adopting a new budget unit. Scope Evaluate conservative display-boundary adjustments for combining marks and joined sequences while keeping the current Unicode-character budget contract explicit. Discuss dependency costs before choosing an algorithm. Acceptance criteria - Use small synthetic cases with combining accents, variation selectors, and joined emoji around both excerpt boundaries. - Never exceed the agreed retained-content limit after adjusting a boundary; explain any under-filled budget. - Keep ordinary ASCII excerpt…
descriptions.github:5680537467: Why this is useful The existing excerpt function keeps a character-counted prefix and suffix, preserving the final exception in long traces. It can nevertheless cut through the middle of a filename, source line, or exception sentence. A line-aware option could make the retained evidence easier to read while retaining the bounded output goal. Exact character slicing remains a reasonable default and is covered by existing tests. Scope Design an optional excerpt strategy that favors complete lines near the head and tail, with a defined fallback for one extremely long line. Acceptance criteria - Compare current and proposed output on a synthetic multiline traceback with a terminal exception. - Define the retained-character budget, marker overhead, and exact omitted-character or omitted-line accounting. - Keep useful content from both ends without duplicating overlapping lines or producing…
descriptions.github:5680536950: Why this is useful The CLI excerpts failure messages and details, but suite, class, test name, and source fields can still be very long. Because Markdown currently includes only complete failure blocks, a large parameterized test name can consume the budget and prevent even a short assertion from appearing. The existing output behavior is documented, so a new display policy should be optional or explicitly reviewed rather than silently changing the contract. Scope Define per-field display limits for Markdown metadata with visible omission markers. Preserve complete structured values in JSON unless a separately agreed policy says otherwise. Acceptance criteria - Use a synthetic parameterized test name and long class/source fields that currently hide a useful short failure. - Keep secret removal before display clipping and avoid cutting generated redaction markers. - Count escaping and…
descriptions.github:5680536433: Why this is useful Sanitization occurs before excerpt , which correctly avoids exposing the raw matched value. However, the excerpt slices arbitrary character positions. A short detail budget applied to TOKEN=[REDACTED] can retain only pieces of the replacement marker around the omission notice. That does not reveal the original secret, but it makes the resulting text look corrupted and obscures whether content was hidden for privacy or shortened for length. Scope Make excerpting treat the generated redaction marker as an indivisible display token while keeping retained-content budgets and omission notices clearly defined. Acceptance criteria - Add a synthetic reproduction with the boundary inside [REDACTED] at both the head and tail. - Specify behavior when the marker is longer than the requested retained-character budget. - Never recover or reintroduce original text to fill an excerpt…
descriptions.github:5680535902: Why this is useful The control sanitizer already removes bidirectional embedding and isolate controls. Its explicit ranges do not include every Unicode directional mark, such as U+061C, U+200E, and U+200F. These marks can affect how mixed-direction failure text appears, but they also have legitimate uses in Arabic and Hebrew text. Expanding deletion without examples would trade one readability problem for another. Scope Create a focused design for these three directional marks: preserve, remove, or visibly annotate them under a documented policy. Do not strip all non-ASCII text. Acceptance criteria - Use synthetic mixed-direction test names and traces, including legitimate Arabic or Hebrew text. - Show the visual or copied-text problem motivating any change and specify default versus opt-in behavior. - Preserve ordinary Unicode content and all existing terminal-control and newline…
descriptions.github:5680535390: Why this is useful A reader currently sees replacement markers but cannot distinguish how many recognized matches were removed, or which broad rule families were involved. Optional summary counts could make it easier to review an output transformation and detect unexpected over-redaction. Such counts must not be presented as proof that the brief is safe: zero matches only means that no supported pattern matched the available fields. Scope Discuss aggregate redaction statistics by a small stable set of categories. Keep raw matched strings, secret lengths, and matching context out of both output and diagnostics. Acceptance criteria - Define whether overlapping patterns count once and how repeated sanitization avoids inflating totals. - Use synthetic fixtures showing zero matches, repeated values, overlapping rules, and multiple failure fields. - Keep metadata optional or versioned and…
descriptions.github:5680534881: Why this is useful Failure traces and report paths can reveal a developer username through paths such as /home/demo-person/project/test.py or C:\Users\DemoPerson\project\test.py . These are not credentials and are intentionally outside the current generic secret patterns. Some users still need to remove that personal context before sharing a brief, while keeping relative project paths useful for debugging. This is separate from normalizing report source paths. Scope Design an explicit privacy option that masks configured home-directory prefixes in every visible failure field, without discovering arbitrary personal files or rewriting paths by default. Acceptance criteria - Cover synthetic POSIX and Windows prefixes, separators, case policy, and paths containing spaces. - Use path-boundary-aware replacement so a short prefix cannot corrupt unrelated filenames or prose. - Preserve enough…
descriptions.github:5680534411: Why this is useful A failure may contain a JSON fragment represented as escaped text, such as {\"password\":\"demo-value\"} where the backslashes are literal characters in the displayed diagnostic. The current redactor operates on the displayed text; it is not an arbitrary decoder. Recursively decoding every field would risk changing useful evidence and creating unpredictable runtime costs. Harmless diagnostics such as token count=17 or secret length=12 are therefore candidates for masking even when the numbers explain the failing assertion. Relaxing this behavior blindly could expose real credentials, so the useful contribution is a small policy change supported by both sensitive and harmless synthetic examples. Scope Discuss a conservative key-boundary or narrow exception policy. Target diagnostic counters rather than introducing a general disable-redaction switch. Acceptance criteria - Provide before/after examples showing the lost debugging information and the intended supported exception. - Include credential names with prefixes, suffixes, hyphens, quotes, and varied case as negative controls. - Keep genuine credential assignments masked and…
descriptions.github:5680533430: Why this is useful A project-specific account number, internal host, or invented credential may not match any built-in heuristic. Users currently cannot supply exact values they already know should disappear. An explicitly selected local literal list could complement the heuristics without adding a regex language or sending report content to another service. This should remain optional because treating broad strings as secrets can destroy useful diagnostic context. Scope Design a small literal-redaction input contract, including encoding, maximum file size, minimum entry length, ordering, and error behavior. Acceptance criteria - Agree on a CLI interface and ensure no file is read unless the user selects it. - Use bounded literal matching and define overlapping, duplicate, blank, and Unicode entry behavior. - Ensure errors…

Acceptance criteria - Construct fake marker names and payloads at runtime; never commit a real or usable private key. - Cover RSA, EC, encrypted, and generic private-key labels within the agreed supported set. - Keep public certificates and ordinary prose unchanged unless an explicitly documented rule applies. - Bound…
descriptions.github:5680532397: Why this is useful The current redactor handles bearer credentials and key-like assignments, but a failure containing Authorization: Basic DEMO VALUE or Cookie: session=demo-value; theme=dark has different structure. A grouped header policy would be easier to review and maintain than unrelated expressions for individual authentication providers. Acceptance criteria - Add synthetic cases for first, middle, repeated, blank, and percent-encoded sensitive query parameters. - Preserve harmless parameters, delimiters, and fragments exactly where the chosen contract permits. - Keep replacement idempotent and cover both standalone URLs and…
descriptions.github:5680531426: Why this would help Reports may be consumed while another process is still writing them. The bounded read already handles growth beyond the byte ceiling, but a same-size rewrite or replacement can produce an inconsistent snapshot without necessarily violating that limit. Proposed scope Investigate best-effort detection of report changes during reading using file-descriptor metadata before and after the read. State the limits of detection rather than promising a filesystem lock or a perfect snapshot. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. descriptions.github:5680523418: Feature Factory Simulation & Abstraction What to Solve? Binary Factorium must run on extremely limited hardware ( ), and thus cannot naively use a tiled simulation or the conventional model. The constrains together make it hard to solve easily. What should the simulator essentially contain or do ideally? It should: - Update O(1) when nothing changes - Update O(n) or O(log(n)) when changes happen (with n = parts to update ) - Not hang when numerous updates happen in a short period of time (also in long periods ideally) - Consume a fixed amount of RAM at any point. - Possibly be asynchronous. - Be Binary-Spectacular ;) I am not an expert in this field ;-; (\ unlike what most factory games with large/infinite world target, Binary Factorium's primary targets are the Fri3d Badges)

Splitting a grapheme cluster in half can make two identical emoji sequences look different, or make a genuinely repeating sequence look distinct. Risky inputs that currently have no fixture coverage: - ZWJ sequences — 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦, 👩‍💻 (variation selector U+FE0F plus U+200D zero-width joiners) - Flag sequences — 🇯🇵 is two regional indicator code points, not one - Combining marks — e + U+0301 versus é as a single code point - RTL text — Arabic or Hebrew inside an otherwise LTR transcript - Emoji with skin-tone modifiers — 👍🏽 is a base plus a modifier If sanitize is not grapheme-aware, that is a real correctness bug in the comparison layer, not just missing tests. descriptions.github:5679932145: The cheapest entry left in the ratchet. Array.prototype.sort() sorts in place , so it mutates the array it was given; toSorted() returns a new one. Why this one is worth doing properly rather than mechanically Two of the three production call sites are in data-table.component.ts , which sorts rows it was handed through an input() . Sorting those in place mutates the caller's array — a signal's value, in most cases — which is how a table can reorder data a parent component still believes it owns, without the parent's signal ever being set. Swapping to toSorted() is the fix, but each site is worth a glance to see whether anything downstream was relying on the mutation. Note toSorted() needs a reasonably current runtime target; it is available in the browsers this project targets and in the Node used for specs. Acceptance - unicorn/no-array-sort is gone from eslint-suppressions.json after…
descriptions.github:5679931860: One of the smaller ratchet entries, and an unusual one: every violation is in a spec file. Production code already goes through the STORAGE adapter; it is the tests that reach localStorage directly. Why it matters more than the count suggests no-restricted-globals exists because Web Storage is a trust boundary ( security.md §4) reached through a global rather than an import, and STORAGE KEYS is meant to be the reviewable inventory of what this origin persists. A spec that writes localStorage directly is also a spec that can pass while the adapter is bypassed — and it leaves state behind for whatever test runs next, since the key never goes through the inventory. What to do Use the fake storage adapter from src/app/testing/adapters ( provideFakeAdapters() ) instead of touching localStorage , and assert against it. A misspelt key - netwrokPolicy: , or connector: for connectors: - is silently ignored. Helm renders the default, the install succeeds, and the setting the operator believes is on is off. descriptions.github:5678907905: 📝 Background ttnn.cumsum has a regression in its compensated FP32 accumulation path. After the running total becomes +inf or -inf—either because an input contains an infinity or because the sum overflows—subsequent output elements become NaN. This behavior diverges from PyTorch: Input: [1.0, inf, 1.0, 1.0] ttnn: [1.0, inf, nan, nan] torch: [1.0, inf, inf, inf] The regression was introduced by the compensated-summation change in 56811. The compensation calculation performs inf - inf, producing NaN; subsequent scan elements are then poisoned. The issue affects the default FP32 path. The existing disable compensated sum=True path avoids the failure but is deprecated and is not an acceptable long-term workaround. 🎯 What Success Looks Like The bounty is complete when all of the following are satisfied: - FP32 ttnn.cumsum preserves IEEE/PyTorch behavior after +inf . - FP32 ttnn.cumsum…

descriptions.github:5677602459: cmd dmesg is a stub. Kernel logs go to serial (and the boot framebuffer early on) but there is no buffer userspace can read back, or if there is one it is not wired to a syscall. First step is checking what DEBUG in src/kernel/debug.h actually emits and whether a ring buffer exists. If not, add a small one behind the existing log path, then an extended syscall that snapshots it out under a lock, then make dmesg print it. Worth deciding what release builds do since most logging is debug only.
descriptions.github:5677600372: cmd lspci in src/usr/shell/shell cmds.cpp prints a stub line. PCI enumeration happens at boot in src/drivers/bus/pci/ but userspace never sees the device list. Needs a new extended syscall (297 or wherever the numbering is by then) that fills an array of small descriptors (bus, slot, function, vendor id, device id, class code) and returns the total count, same shape as SYS INPUT ENUM DEVICES. Then the builtin just prints the table. include/uapi/input.h plus the input enum case in src/kernel/core/syscall.cpp are the reference for the uapi side.
descriptions.github:5677599797: There is no netstat. The TCP and UDP tables live in src/net/tcp.cpp and src/net/udp.cpp but nothing exports counts to userspace (sockets in use, per state, rx/tx bytes). Simplest version is a small extended syscall filling a struct with tcp and udp socket counts per state, next free number is 297. sys net status in src/net/net.cpp is the pattern to copy, and the input enum devices case in src/kernel/core/syscall.cpp shows the array-plus-count shape. Then a netstat builtin in src/usr/shell/shell cmds.cpp that prints it. The socket tables are plain arrays so ktesting the counters is easy.
descriptions.github:5677599522: Every UDP socket has one 1500 byte receive slot with overwrite semantics (src/net/udp.cpp). If two datagrams land before the app calls recvfrom the first one is gone, and nothing reports it either. Turning the slot into a small ring, 4 entries or so, would fix the common case. The receive handoff runs inside net poll() under the table spinlock so the write path has to stay cheap, a memcpy into a preallocated ring is fine. Some way to see overflow would be good too, a debug warn or a dropped counter.
descriptions.github:5677599224: Every resolve goes out on the wire even when we just resolved the same name. dns resolve() in src/net/dns.cpp already retries three times with fresh transaction ids, there is just no cache anywhere. A small table of the last few answers with a short TTL (30-60 seconds is plenty for this stack) would do. The resolver runs from syscall context so keep it under the existing locks. A ktest for expiry and eviction can go next to the dns tests in src/net/dns tests.cpp.

descriptions.github:5676728882: Why Some searches expand a tree of decisions one ply at a time: a game, a plan, a sequence of tool calls. The full tree does not fit, and there is no stored graph. Monte Carlo tree search keeps the branches it has tried, picks the next one with an upper confidence bound, and backs a score up the path. 133 covers finding a path through a successor function. This issue is the tree of sampled decisions on top of that idea. Proposed API In a new package search : Options: - WithIterations(n int) , default 100. - WithExploration(c float64) , default math.Sqrt2 . This is the UCB1 constant. - WithRand(r rand.Rand) . When nil, each rollout picks a uniform legal action with crypto/rand . A non-nil source makes the search reproducible. Behavior - A nil actions , next , or score returns an error. - WithIterations below 1 returns an error. - Selection walks from the root by UCB1 until it reaches a…
descriptions.github:5676728489: Why Nearest-neighbor search for retrieval keeps a stack of graphs. The top layer is sparse. The bottom layer contains every point. A search starts at the top, greedily walks to a closer neighbor, then drops a layer. That is the HNSW search. The points stay in the caller's table. The graph stores ids, because a vector is not a comparable label in any useful way. This issue is the layered graph and the greedy search. It is not a database. There is no index file, no metadata filter, and no delete. Proposed API A new package nn : Behavior - distance must be zero or positive. A negative distance returns an error at search or insert time. - m and efConstruction below 1 return an error from New . A nil distance returns an error. - k or ef below 1 returns an error from Search . - Insert of an id that is already present does nothing and returns nil. - The neighbor sets are chosen by the HNSW…
descriptions.github:5676728256: Why Some DAGs accept a vertex only after several successful samples, and only after its parents are accepted. Avalanche counts confidence that way. The sample itself is a network call. The library can own the counter and the parent rule. The caller owns the query. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed acyclic graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected or gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - sample , beta , or rounds below 1 returns an error. A nil query returns an error. - Parents are incoming neighbors. - A vertex with no parents may be accepted on its own run of successes. - A failed query resets that vertex's consecutive count to 0. It does not reset other vertices. - The result is in GetAllVertices order, and contains only accepted vertices. - Returned vertices are the graph's own pointers. - The function does not open a connection, pick peers, or sign anything. query is the whole…
descriptions.github:5676728025: Why A block DAG is not a chain. One way to order it is to paint a well-connected subset blue and leave the rest red. A set is a k-cluster when every member has at most k other members that it cannot reach and that cannot reach it. The largest such set is expensive to find. The greedy coloring used by GHOSTDAG walks in topological order and adds a vertex to the blue set when the blue anticone is still within k. This is that coloring. It is not a node, and it does not choose a block for a peer to mine on. HeaviestBranch is the walk on a tree. This is the coloring on a DAG. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed acyclic graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected or gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - k below 0 returns dag.ErrInvalidK . - Two vertices are incomparable when neither can reach the other. - The walk order is the stable topological order, the same one TopologySort returns. - A…
descriptions.github:5676727781: Why Some DAGs decide that event A has seen event B only when the paths between them cover a supermajority of authors. Hashgraph calls this strongly seeing. The predicate is ancestor counting. Virtual voting and witness election stay with the caller. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected . - members below 1 returns an error. A nil author returns an error. - Missing from or to: gograph.ErrVertexDoesNotExist . - Seeing is reachability along directed edges, including a vertex seeing itself. - The threshold is strictly greater than 2 members/3 . For 4 members the threshold is more than 8/3, so 3 authors. The test should use that case. - Authors are compared with == . The function does not check that every author id is one of a fixed set. An author outside the expected set still counts as one distinct author, which can only make the count…
descriptions.github:5676727518: Why Fork choice on a tree of blocks walks from the root and, at each block, follows the child whose subtree carries the most weight. GHOST and LMD-GHOST are that walk. The weight is whatever the caller counts: work, stake, or the latest vote of each validator. The library does not know which. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected . - A vertex with two incoming edges, or a vertex not reachable from root, returns dag.ErrNotTree . - A cycle returns gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - Subtree weight is the vertex's own weight plus the subtree weights of its children. A vertex is not counted twice. - Ties break by GetAllVertices order of the children. - The returned path starts at root and ends at a leaf. Vertices are the graph's own pointers. - Negative weights are allowed. They only change which child wins. - Missing root…
descriptions.github:5676727251: Why Max flow ( 193) asks how much can move. Some networks also have a price on each edge. Splitting a payment across channels is the usual case: send a given amount, stay inside each edge's capacity, and pay the least fee. Proposed API In flow , beside MaxFlow : Successive shortest paths with potentials. Costs may be negative. A negative cycle in the residual graph returns flow.ErrNegativeCycle . Behavior - amount below 0 returns an error. amount of 0 returns a shipment of value 0 and cost 0. - A negative capacity returns flow.ErrNegativeCapacity . - Missing source or sink: gograph.ErrVertexDoesNotExist . - Directed edges carry flow in their direction. An undirected edge shares its capacity across the two directions, and that capacity is not doubled. - For every vertex other than source and sink, flow in equals flow out. - Flow on an edge stays inside its capacity. - Among shipments of…
descriptions.github:5676726980: Why Clustering merges labels into groups as pairs arrive: two addresses that shared an input, two records that are the same entity. Building a graph first is an extra copy. Disjoint sets answer "are these the same group" in nearly constant time. Proposed API A new package unionfind : Union by rank and path compression. Behavior - Connected on a label that was never seen is false. - Union of a label with itself adds it and leaves it in a group of one. - Representatives are deterministic for a given sequence of calls. - Groups does not return a representative that the caller has to interpret. It returns the members. - The package does not know about graphs. A caller with a graph passes labels. Tests - Five unions that form two groups. Connected matches. Groups matches, in insertion order. - Path compression does not change Connected results. - Find on an unknown label returns false…
descriptions.github:5676726745: Why Some DAGs are ordered by a score that includes the ancestors, not by the vertex alone. A transaction pool ranks a transaction by the total fee of itself and everything that must come before it, divided by the total size of that same set. StableTopologySort can compare vertices, and it cannot see that sum. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed acyclic graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected or gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - The set for a vertex is itself plus every vertex that can reach it. - The key is the sum of num over that set, divided by the sum of den over that set. - A denominator sum of 0 returns dag.ErrZeroDenominator . - Ties break by GetAllVertices order. - Returned vertices are the graph's own pointers, one per vertex in the graph. - Empty graph: nil, nil. - This is a ranking, not a topological order. A later vertex can rank ahead of an ancestor. Callers who need a…
descriptions.github:5676726508: Why Callers often need the best few items, not a full ordering. A mempool keeps the highest-paying transactions. A ranking keeps the top vertices by score. Retrieval keeps the nearest matches. A full sort does more work than that, and it allocates a second copy of the whole list. Proposed API In util : Behavior - k below 0 returns util.ErrInvalidK . k of 0 returns an empty slice and a nil error. - A nil better returns an error. - A nil or empty items returns an empty slice. - The result is a new slice. items is left as it was. - Equal items keep their original order. - Running time is linear in the length of items times log of k , using a heap of size k . The doc comment says so. A caller who wants a nucleus-style prefix computes it from this ordered prefix. The function does not grow a sampling API. Tests - Ten integers, k of 3, the three largest in order. - Ties: two equal best items…
descriptions.github:5676726283: Why AStar ( 185) keeps every unsettled vertex in a heap. When the frontier is large, the memory is the problem. Iterative deepening A repeats a depth-first search with a rising limit on the estimated total cost, and stores only the current path. Planners use it when the graph of states does not fit in memory. Proposed API In path , with the same cost and heuristic contract as AStar : Behavior - Costs must be zero or positive. A negative cost returns path.ErrNegativeWeight . - The search raises the limit to the smallest f-value that was beyond the previous limit. - It returns a cheapest path when the heuristic is admissible. The doc comment says so. It does not check the heuristic. - Missing vertices, an unreachable goal, and start equal to goal follow AStar . - Ties break by vertex and edge order. - The doc comment says AStar is the better choice when the frontier fits in memory…
descriptions.github:5676725921: Why On a graph that branches widely, keeping every partial path is too expensive. Beam search keeps a fixed number of them and drops the rest. Decoders use it to keep a few partial sequences. The same bound keeps a path search inside a memory limit. The result can miss the cheapest path. That is the trade. Proposed API In path : Behavior - width below 1 returns path.ErrInvalidWidth . - Partial paths are simple. A vertex is not repeated on one path. - At each step the search keeps the width partial paths with the best score. Ties break by vertex order. - If the goal is never among the kept paths, path.ErrUnreachable . - Missing start or goal: gograph.ErrVertexDoesNotExist . - start equals goal: a one-vertex path and cost 0, for any positive width. - Returned vertices are the graph's own pointers. - The same graph, width, and score give the same path on every run. - The doc comment says a…
descriptions.github:5676725632: Why A route from one vertex to one other vertex does not need a distance for every vertex. Searching forward from the start and backward from the goal meets in the middle and settles fewer vertices on a large graph. Payment-channel routing and road routing both do this. Proposed API In path , beside AStar ( 185): Behavior - Directed graphs: the backward search walks incoming edges. Undirected graphs: either direction. - Missing start or goal: gograph.ErrVertexDoesNotExist . - Unreachable: path.ErrUnreachable . - start equals goal: a one-vertex path and cost 0. - A negative cost: path.ErrNegativeWeight . - The path vertices are the graph's own pointers, start first and goal last. - Ties break by the order vertices and edges were added. - The two searches stop once the cheapest meeting point is settled. They do not scan the whole graph when the goal is close. Tests - A path graph where…

descriptions.github:5676656749: Research has no connector for the two stock libraries users ask for most. This is a known limitation: "Keyed stock libraries (Pexels, Pixabay…) have no built-in connector — as website sources they are searched through the web backend and most of their media is JS-rendered." As a site source, a Pexels or Pixabay URL goes through the DuckDuckGo web backend and the static page inspector, which finds almost nothing on their JS-rendered pages. Maintainer decision: add built-in Pexels and Pixabay connectors that use the user's own API key (each provider issues a free key); the key never enters the Asset Search policy file because that file is served to the webview. Ground rules Read AGENTS.md first. For this task: - A source is data: a connector plus the domains it lives on ( TrustedSource , packages/agent-protocol/src/research.ts:46-64 ). Adding a provider is one connector file plus one…
descriptions.github:5676656456: The research download cache /.hyperframes/research/cache/ is never pruned: every URL imported by Research leaves its bytes (one file per sha256) plus index.json in the project, and reverting the turn that imported the asset keeps the cache on purpose (it sits outside history — packages/studio-server/src/helpers/projectSignature.ts:193-196 , asserted by projectSignature.test.ts:84-86 ). A project's cache therefore only grows, and today the user has no way to reclaim that disk space. This is a known limitation. Maintainer decision: no automatic cleanup ever (no TTL, no size cap, no pruning on revert) — the only cleanup is an explicit user action in the app. Ground rules Read AGENTS.md first. For this task: - The cache is project state on disk and a pure cache: deleting it may only cost a re-download. It must never touch assets/research/ (the imported files) or…

This issue adds it: one chat per file, a versioned JSON document, importable into any project, with the transcript intact and the chat still continuable. descriptions.github:5673427734: Current behavior 🐛 BorderVisual (Skia) replaces its RectangleClip objects whenever the border or corner radius geometry changes, but never disposes the old ones. In UpdatePathsAndCornerClip() , the old childClipCausedByCornerRadius and backgroundClip are just set to null and new clips are created (L203-L212, L330-L346). Since 24230, RectangleClip caches one geometry (a native SKPath ) and only releases it in DisposeInternal() (RectangleClip.skia.cs L42). Nothing calls Dispose() on a replaced clip, so its cached path is freed only by the SKPath finalizer when the GC gets around to it, not deterministically. Impact is low: it is bounded to one path per replaced clip and the finalizer does clean it up eventually. descriptions.github:5673397362: Summary message validator.enabled is converted with bool(...) , so a quoted YAML string enables the validator instead of disabling it. Currently becomes message validator=True because bool("false") is True . Real YAML false correctly disables it. Why this matters Operators who quote booleans (common when templating YAML) think they turned the validator off; Mycelium silently turns it on. Same class of bug as 130. Expected behavior When present, message validator.enabled must be an actual YAML boolean. Strings, numbers, and null must raise ConfigError . Suggested scope - Replace bool(message validator raw.get("enabled", True)) in sdk/mycelium/config parser.py with an isinstance(..., bool) check. - Preserve message validator: true/false shorthand if that path already exists. - Add parser regression tests. Acceptance criteria - Quoted "true" / "false" are rejected. - Integers such as 0 / 1…
descriptions.github:5673397108: Summary Redis/Postgres action-ledger timing fields are converted with bare float(...) and are not checked for finiteness or boolean type. These currently load successfully: Why this matters in flight ttl is a primary-key TTL used for crash recovery; retention seconds supplies the default prune window. Non-finite or boolean values produce silent misconfiguration of retention and recovery timing. Acceptance criteria - NaN and ±Infinity are rejected for both…
descriptions.github:5673396892: Summary destructive confirm.tools. .grant.ttl seconds rejects booleans and non-positive numbers, but still accepts NaN and positive Infinity because the check is only value < = 0 (NaN comparisons are false; +inf < = 0 is false). These currently load successfully: Why this matters Grant TTL controls how long a destructive confirmation remains valid. descriptions.github:5670506268: --jobs is validated (--jobs must be at least 1, exit 3), and the decay-day flags use non negative int, but --limit and --min-contributors use plain type=int: --limit -5 silently scans zero issues and exits 0 with a 'no open issues found' note, and --min-contributors -3 is silently meaningless. --explore-floor takes any float even though it is a probability (default 0.15). The same gap exists on the MCP side: discover candidates accepts negative pr idle days / claim silence days / claim silence complex days with no validation, and scan repo(limit=-5) returns an all-zero summary indistinguishable from a genuinely empty repo. Expected: the same non-negative (and range) validation the codebase already applies to the other numeric inputs. Evidence: - taken/cli.py:74 - taken/cli.py:98 - taken/cli.py:126 - taken/cli.py:50 - taken/mcp server.py:157 - taken/mcp server.py:252 Expected behavior…
descriptions.github:5670505846: Unparseable targets go through parse error, which deliberately returns exit code 3 (the code comments that a usage error must exit 3 without touching the network). But --discover given targets and --health given bad targets go through argparse parser.error, which exits 2. Scripts or agents that distinguish exit 3 as the usage-error contract get mixed signals depending on which flag was misused. Expected: one consistent exit code for all usage errors. This is low impact since both codes are nonzero, but the codebase states its own contract and then violates it in two paths. Evidence: - taken/cli.py:41 - taken/cli.py:372 - taken/cli.py:378 - taken/cli.py:380 Expected behavior: Use one consistent usage-error exit code across all CLI paths, matching the documented contract of 3 from the parse error comment. Why it matters: Scripts and agents key off exit codes, including our own scout…
descriptions.github:5670504865: The scan issue claims docstring describes a claim as waiting when it is older than claim wait days, but waiting entry and quiet entry return entries when age days == wait days (they only reject age days < wait days). The inclusive boundary is arguably the better behavior, but the docstring and code disagree by one day; pick one and make both match. Evidence: - taken/health.py:212 - taken/health.py:178 - taken/health.py:196 Expected behavior: Pick one boundary and make the docstring match the code. The inclusive code behavior looks like the right one to keep. Why it matters: One-day disagreements between docs and code are exactly how the next contributor introduces a real off-by-one. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.
descriptions.github:5670503339: truncated is computed as len(issues) = options.issue limit, so a repo with exactly issue limit open issues and nothing more is flagged as truncated even though the listing is complete. The flag should only be set when there is evidence of more data, for example when a full final page was returned. Minor, but it can send a maintainer looking for issues that do not exist. Evidence: - taken/health.py:349 Expected behavior: Set truncated only when there is evidence of more data, for example a full final page, instead of the = comparison against issue limit. Why it matters: A false truncated flag sends a maintainer hunting for issues that do not exist. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.
descriptions.github:5670501677: pace search is defined but never called anywhere in the audited files; the live pacing path is wait search pace called from gh api run while holding search lock. Dead code carrying a docstring that describes live behavior risks a future reader wiring it in (which would double-pace searches) or relying on behavior that is never exercised. It should be removed or covered by a test that pins the intended pacing contract. Evidence: - taken/checks.py:437 Expected behavior: Remove the dead helper, or pin it with a test if it is meant to be the future pacing contract. It should not sit there looking live while nothing calls it. Why it matters: Dead code with a live-sounding docstring misleads the next reader into wiring it in, which would double-pace searches. Keep the codebase honest. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.

descriptions.github:5670344064: Problem yaatv currently emits its low-bitrate source warning whenever the detected bitrate is below the configured threshold. That warning is useful for lossy sources such as MP3 or AAC, but it can be misleading for lossless formats such as FLAC, ALAC, WAV, or AIFF. A lossless source can have a comparatively low bitrate because of its content or compression efficiency without representing degraded source quality. Requested behavior Only emit the low-bitrate source-quality warning when the source codec/format is one where bitrate is a meaningful quality signal. The change should: - preserve the existing warning for applicable lossy sources; - avoid the warning for clearly lossless sources such as FLAC, ALAC, WAV, and AIFF; - keep the existing warning threshold unchanged; - add focused unit tests for both lossy and lossless cases; - preserve --no-warn behavior. Current workaround Users of…

descriptions.github:5670236246: Problem When yaatv generates the default output filename, it reads artist/title metadata from the audio file. The current artist lookup recognizes values such as artist , albumartist , ID3 TPE1 , and MP4 ©ART , but some supported containers expose equivalent artist metadata under other common keys. In particular: - MP4/M4A can use aART for album artist; - ASF/WMA commonly uses Author . When those are the only populated artist fields, yaatv can fall back to the source filename instead of producing the expected Artist - Title.mp4 default name. Requested behavior Extend artist metadata lookup so the default output-name path also recognizes the relevant MP4 and ASF/WMA artist aliases. At minimum: - recognize MP4 aART ; - recognize ASF/WMA Author ; - preserve the current precedence for existing artist fields; - keep title handling unchanged unless a format-specific test shows a corresponding…

The test should follow the style of the existing default and square-output integration tests rather than introducing new fixture…

Bizarrap" or "A, B & C" — one row per song can never answer "show me every song by B". There is even a TODO about this in AudioStoreDataSource.kt:82-87 . The web version already solved the parsing ( origin/legacy:src/lib/stores/artist.svelte.ts ); the native app should port that semantics into real tables instead of re-deriving it in memory. Port exactly this behavior: What to do - PR1 — schema + sync: artists(id auto, name, normalizedName UNIQUE, coverUri?) + song artists(songId, artistId) junction. Parse during the library sync inside a Room transaction on Dispatchers.IO . Note: only the primary artist has a MediaStore ARTIST ID — collaborators get synthetic ids keyed by normalized name, so design for that from the start. - PR2 — wire the artists screen to the…
descriptions.github:5670086592: Context The web version ( legacy branch) exported playlists to a JSON backup copied to the clipboard, and could import it back ( origin/legacy:src/lib/db/backup.ts ). Users migrating to the native app would love their playlists to travel with them — and the format is fully documented in the old code, so no guesswork is needed. The legacy format: - songIds are MediaStore ids stored as text (see origin/legacy:src/lib/db/db/schema.ts : song id TEXT ). - Import matched playlists by name , skipped already-present songs, and mapped name == "favoritos" && id == 1 to favorites. What to do - Single PR: "import backup" entry point (paste-from-clipboard, mirroring the legacy UX) that parses the JSON above, validates formatVersion , and matches each songId against the current device MediaStore library. - Songs not found on this device must be reported, not silently dropped (e.g. "3 of 42 songs not…
descriptions.github:5670084875: Context Playlists today are List(10) placeholders in features/playlists/presentation/playlists.kt : the empty state is unreachable, both FABs are dead ( onClick = {} ), and there is no persistence at all. Room is half-declared — room-ktx is in app/build.gradle.kts but room-compiler is absent, so zero / can compile. The favorites design decision lives separately in 16 (read it first: kind column, not the "favoritos" sentinel). The legacy schema ( origin/legacy:src/lib/db/db/schema.ts ) is the porting reference: playlists(id, name, date created) + playlists songs(id, playlist id FK cascade, song id TEXT) — note song id is text (MediaStore id as string) and the old table lacked a uniqueness constraint, which once forced a duplicate cleanup. What to do - PR1 — Room setup done right: add room-compiler + KSP config in the same commit as the entities (compiler alone or entities alone means…
descriptions.github:5670083422: Context The web version ( legacy branch) stored favorites as a playlist literally named "favoritos" (id 1). The native app inherited the hack: playlists.kt hardcodes a "favoritos" sentinel row. If the user renames that playlist, favorites silently "disappear", and any playlist the user names favoritos collides with it. What to do When introducing Room (see the playlists persistence issue), model this properly instead of porting the sentinel: - playlists table gets a kind column: NORMAL / FAVORITES , with a constraint/guarantee that exactly one FAVORITES row exists. - Migration path: a legacy row named "favoritos" becomes kind = FAVORITES , not a name match. - Export keeps writing name: "favoritos", id: 1 in the backup JSON, so backups produced by the new app remain readable by the old app (forward compat for free). descriptions.github:5669579562: What happened? The COMPOSABLE scoring tent currently penalizes modules with extreme stability ($I = 0.00$), dropping their score to 0%. While this penalty makes sense for high-level orchestration modules, it creates a false positive penalty for leaf utility files (e.g., basic UI components, data structures, or primitive helpers) that are intended to have zero efferent coupling ($C e = 0$). Example Scenario 1. A foundational UI file ( menu.rs ) has low initial coupling ($C a + C e < 2$), causing Topos to fall back to a neutral $I = 0.50$ midpoint score (quality = 1.0, overall score 80%). 2. Additional features adopt menu.rs , raising afferent coupling ($C a \ge 2$). 3. Because menu.rs relies on no other internal modules ($C e = 0$), its instability now resolves to $I = 0.00$. 4. Result: Topos penalizes the file for extreme stability, dropping its score from 80% to 0.0% and triggering a…

descriptions.github:5669261268: Problem - Users walk away from slow requests. Local models are slow, so users switch to something else during long requests and don't know when one finishes or needs approval. - Long-running processes block the model. It can't start a dev server or a test watcher and keep working, because bash waits for the command to end, or times out. Proposal - Notifications: a desktop notification when a request that took longer than N seconds finishes, or when it waits for approval. - It uses notify-send on Linux and osascript on macOS, with the terminal bell as a fallback. - Settings: notify = on | off and the time threshold. - Good first issue. - Background commands: bash with background: true starts a process and returns an id. - bash output(id) reads its new output and bash stop(id) stops it. - Background processes are stopped when the session ends and listed in /jobs . Acceptance criteria - […

Edits go through the editor's buffers. - Later: a dedicated VS Code extension, if ACP support there isn't enough. descriptions.github:5669258945: Problem On an unfamiliar codebase, the model spends many steps and tokens discovering its structure. grep finds exact words, not ideas such as "where do we retry failed uploads?". Proposal - Repository map: a compact, ranked outline of the repository's important symbols (classes, functions, signatures, extracted with tree-sitter). - Symbols are ranked by how often they're referenced, like aider's repo map, and the map is cut to a token budget. - Small repositories get it in the system prompt; larger ones through a repo map tool. - Semantic search: code chunks are indexed with a local embedding model through Ollama (such as qwen3-embedding or nomic-embed-text ). - The index lives in lcode's state folder and updates as files change. - A search code(query) tool returns the best matches with file:line . - All local: the index size and model are configurable. lcode index builds or refreshes…
descriptions.github:5669258558: Problem The model navigates code with grep: - It's imprecise in large codebases , where the same names appear everywhere. - Type errors surface late. The model only learns about them when it runs the build. - Wasted reads cost more with less context. With a small context window, every unnecessary file read is expensive. Proposal - Tools backed by language servers: definition , references , symbols (in a file or the workspace) and hover (type or signature). - Language servers include pyright or basedpyright, typescript-language-server, gopls, rust-analyzer and clangd. - They start on demand and are reused within the session. - Diagnostics after edits: collect diagnostics for each edited file, and add new errors to the tool result ("edit applied; 2 new type errors: …"), so the model fixes them right away. - Setup: detect installed servers and list them in lcode doctor ; configurable per…

descriptions.github:5668905028: Right now in a training run, all the dimer configurations in a node are sent to compute the energy by the force routines one by one. If we have 1000 dimer conformations for water-water, the force routines are called 1000 times. This prevents optimisation, let alone porting to GPUs. The first step to optimise this would be that the force routines should be called once and handle 1000 dimers. This would allow using SIMD on CPUs and gives us 3-8 times the performance we have now for training. To be able to do this, the deviation from the reference has to be computed at once. The next step would be to run all the dimers on a node in a single force call rather than one per dimer. If that is possible it may be feasible to port to GPUs.
